If you need localised error text on the consumer side, branch on the code of each entry of the response’s errors array (see ferra-error-handling.md § Validation codes) and rewrite the message client-side; do not match on the message text. SDK consumers that have to rewrite the body server-side can do so in a Tower middleware layer applied after the framework’s IntoResponse runs.

Unicode counting

Length rules count characters as the underlying validation crate counts them: chars().count() on the underlying &str, which counts Unicode scalar values. The framework does not interpose a custom counting policy in 0.6.0 — there is no NFC normalisation pass, no grapheme-cluster counting, no UTF-16 code-unit counting.

The practical consequence: a 10-emoji string may not have a length of 10 by your reader’s intuition. The grinning-face emoji 😀 is one scalar value (one chars() count), but some emoji sequences (skin-tone modifiers, ZWJ-joined family emoji) are several scalar values — a single visible glyph may count as 2, 4, or more. If your length rule needs to count “what the user sees”, reach for the typed-escape path below and write a hand-rolled rule that walks unicode-segmentation graphemes.

When the eight rules are not enough — typed escape via ferra::garde

The eight-rule namespace is a closed contract surface for 0.6.0. For rule shapes the surface does not cover — a custom function predicate, a locale-aware rule, a regex syntax beyond the regex crate, a grapheme-cluster-aware length count — Ferra re-exports the underlying validation crate at ferra::garde so you can hand-roll a garde::Validate impl on your model:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::garde::{self, Validate};

// `MyModel` is a model of yours that carries no `#[field(...)]` rule.
struct MyModel;

impl Validate for MyModel {
    type Context = ();

    fn validate_into(
        &self,
        _ctx: &Self::Context,
        _parent: &mut dyn FnMut() -> garde::Path,
        report: &mut garde::error::Report,
    ) {
        // your hand-rolled checks here, appending to `report`
    }
}
}

The escape is the documented fallback — neither encouraged nor forbidden, used when the closed set is insufficient. It is not part of the v1 #[field(...)] contract surface; the rule shape and the trait surface follow the upstream garde crate’s evolution, not Ferra’s. Use it sparingly: every model that hand-rolls validation is a model the #[field(...)] diagnostics no longer protect.

Hand-rolling a Validate impl on a model that ALSO carries #[field(...)] rules is a duplicate-impl error at compile time. The two paths are exclusive: either the framework generates the impl from your declarative rules, or you write it yourself.

Primary keys

The server chooses the key of a new row, unless the model says otherwise:

  • a single i32 / i64 key: the database (SERIAL or an identity column). Do not mark it auto_increment = false.
  • a single Uuid / ferra::Id key: Ferra generates a UUID v7.
  • anything else — a composite key, a natural key (String), an integer the client assigns — needs #[ferra(client_pk)]: the create body carries every key field, and the update body never does (the path names the row).

Without client_pk, a key the server cannot generate does not compile (FRG-319). A key field in a projection’s write = [...] list does not compile either (FRG-318): the key is never written by an update.

Composite primary keys

A model can carry two or more #[sea_orm(primary_key)] markers; it then needs #[ferra(client_pk)].

A worked example with (tenant_id: Uuid, document_id: i64):

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(
    Clone, Debug, PartialEq,
    DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel,
    Serialize, Deserialize,
)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "documents")]
#[ferra(auth = "none", client_pk)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key, auto_increment = false)]
    pub tenant_id: Uuid,
    #[sea_orm(primary_key, auto_increment = false)]
    pub document_id: i64,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

#[sea_orm(auto_increment = false)] is required on every PK field in a composite key — PostgreSQL SERIAL only synthesises a value for one column per table, so the application supplies an explicit value on every insert.

A route of your own reads a row of such a model through Resource<M>: the key is the tuple of the key fields, in declaration order.

use axum::{Json, extract::Path};
use ferra::{FerraError, Resource};
use ferra::model::FerraViews;
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod document {
    use super::*;
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "documents")]
    #[ferra(auth = "none", client_pk)]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key, auto_increment = false)]
        pub tenant_id: Uuid,
        #[sea_orm(primary_key, auto_increment = false)]
        pub document_id: i64,
        pub title: String,
    }
    #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
    pub enum Relation {}
    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}
use document::Model as Document;
async fn one(
    docs: Resource<Document>,
    Path((tenant_id, document_id)): Path<(Uuid, i64)>,
) -> Result<Json<<Document as FerraViews>::Read>, FerraError> {
    Ok(Json(docs.get((tenant_id, document_id)).await?))
}
fn main() {}

The framework derives:

SurfaceSingle-PK shapeComposite-PK shape (2 keys)
Per-item routeGET /films/{id}GET /documents/{tenant_id}/{document_id}
Location header on POST/films/{id}/documents/{tenant_id}/{document_id}
_links.self.href/films/{id}/documents/{tenant_id}/{document_id}
OpenAPI parameters count1 entry2 entries (in declaration order)

The path segments follow the #[sea_orm(primary_key)] declaration order in the struct ((Uuid, i64) for the Document entity above). Reordering the markers in the source struct is therefore a wire-breaking change for any client URL-templating against _links.self.href or against the OpenAPI path template.

The _links.self.href shape on a fetched row:

{
  "_links": {
    "self":       { "href": "https://api.example.com/documents/<tenant>/<doc>" },
    "collection": { "href": "https://api.example.com/documents" }
  }
}

Ferra supports any N >= 1. A three-key composite ((tenant_id, year, sequence)) emits GET /issued_documents/{tenant_id}/{year}/{sequence} with three OpenAPI parameters. The framework does not impose an upper bound; in practice 2-4 keys cover the working set (multi-tenant isolation, time-bucketed sequencing, partition keys). The N=0 case continues to fail at compile time with the existing “this model has no primary key” diagnostic — composite primary keys are a widening of the legacy single-PK rule, not a relaxation.

The body of an action: #[derive(ferra::ActionBody)]

An action that takes a value (action(.., body = ProgressBody, ..), ADR-0080) types it with a struct that derives ActionBody next to Deserialize. The derive reads the struct’s fields once and that one list is what Ferra uses to refuse a key the struct does not declare (422 unknown_field), to validate the values with Ferra’s own messages, and to describe the request body in the OpenAPI document (additionalProperties: false, the validation keywords, required). A body = T whose T lacks the derive does not compile: the error says add #[derive(ferra::ActionBody)] to T and points at body = T.

use ferra::ActionBody;
use serde::Deserialize;
#[derive(Deserialize, ActionBody)]
pub struct ProgressBody {
    #[field(min = 0, max = 100)]
    pub progress: i32,
    #[field(max_length = 200)]
    pub note: Option<String>,
}
fn main() {}

What a body admits, and no more:

  • Scalar fields: a String, i32, i64, f64, bool, a Uuid or ferra::Id, a ferra::DateTime, ferra::Date or ferra::Time, or an Option of one of them. No nested object, no JSON value, no Vec (FRG-145).
  • The eight validation keys of #[field(...)] (min_length, max_length, min, max, pattern, email, url, required), as for a model. Any other key is FRG-145.
  • A field that is not an Option is required by its type. A body that leaves it out is a 400 invalid_json, because it does not deserialize, and not the 422 required of a PUT. See Declared actions.
  • No #[serde(...)] attribute, on the struct or on a field: the wire name of a field is its Rust name (FRG-116 for a rename or a reshaping attribute, FRG-145 for the others).
  • No new dependency: the application writes Deserialize as it does for a model and names neither garde nor utoipa.

Why DeriveEntityModel is required

Skipping the DeriveEntityModel sibling is a class-16 compile error:

error: FerraModel requires DeriveEntityModel on the same struct
         help: add DeriveEntityModel to the `#[derive(...)]` list
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-016
  --> src/models/film.rs:3:12
   |
 3 | pub struct Film {
   |            ^^^^

The requirement is not decorative. Phase 0.3.0 Casting wires the Entity, Column, PrimaryKey, and ActiveModel types that DeriveEntityModel generates into the router and SQL query builder. A FerraModel-only struct would compile locally but collapse the moment ferra-http or ferra-db touches it. The rule fails loud now so you cannot paint yourself into that corner.

Troubleshooting

Every error class 0.2.0 emits, with the exact message shape and the fix. Numbering matches data-model.md § 4 of the Smelting spec.

About the rendered shape. Every Ferra-authored diagnostic in this section carries three logical lines — an error: line, a help: line, and a note: line — because ferra-forge builds them as a single syn::Error on stable Rust. The help and note appear as indented continuation lines of the error body rather than as separate = help: / = note: sub-lines (that shape requires proc_macro::Diagnostic, which is nightly-only as of the 2026-04 toolchain). Text content is identical; grep-based CI checks and visual legibility both work.

Class 1 — no primary key (FRG-001)

error: FRG-001: this model has no primary key
         help: annotate at least one field `#[sea_orm(primary_key)]`
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-001

Fix. Add #[sea_orm(primary_key)] to the id field. Several fields may carry it: composite primary keys are supported (since 0.6.0).

Class 2 — historical (multiple primary keys — retired in 0.6.0; FRG-002 is intentionally unallocated)

Several fields may carry #[sea_orm(primary_key)]: composite primary keys are supported since 0.6.0 (see § Composite primary keys). The diagnostic that previously fired here (“composite primary keys are not supported in Ferra 0.2.0”) no longer exists, and no code replaces it. The class number is preserved for historical reference.

Class 3 — unsupported field type (FRG-003)

error: FRG-003: type `Vec < String >` is not supported by Ferra
         help: use one of `String`, `i32`, `i64`, `f64`, `bool`, `Uuid` (or `ferra::Id`), `ferra::DateTime`, `ferra::Date`, `ferra::Time`, `serde_json::Value` (or `Json`), or `Option<T>` of any of them; a serde type stored as JSON takes `#[field(json)]`
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-003

Fix. Use one of the recognised field types below.

Recognised field types

String, i32, i64, f64, bool, Uuid or ferra::Id, ferra::DateTime, ferra::Date, ferra::Time, serde_json::Value or Json, and Option<T> of each. Time values from chrono, time or jiff are refused with a dedicated message: use the Ferra types (see ferra-core.md § Time vocabulary). A struct of your own stored as JSON (Sea-ORM’s FromJsonQueryResult) is a field type once it carries #[field(json)]; sea_orm::Value is a SQL value, not a document (ferra-core.md § JSON documents).

Class 4 — historical (Option<Uuid> rejection — retired in 0.6.0; FRG-004 is intentionally unallocated)

Option<Uuid> and Option<Id> are now first-class field types admitted as FieldType::OptionUuid (0.6.0 Welding User Story 4 — FR-014). The diagnostic that previously fired here (“Option<Uuid> is not supported in Ferra 0.2.0”) no longer exists. The class number is preserved for historical reference; the contradictory case Option<Uuid> tagged #[sea_orm(primary_key)] is now rejected with FRG-215 instead — shape and fix below.

error: FRG-215: primary key cannot be optional
         help: primary key fields must always have a value; remove `Option<...>` from the field type or remove `#[sea_orm(primary_key)]` from the field tag
         note: an inserted `None` would be indistinguishable from a row whose key was never assigned, so the round-trip equality semantics a PK guarantees cannot hold; see Spec §Edge Cases "Optional UUID field tagged as primary key"
  --> src/film.rs:6:9
   |
 6 |     pub id: Option<Uuid>,
   |         ^^

Fix. Either drop the Option<...> from the field type (so the PK is always present), or remove #[sea_orm(primary_key)] from the tag (so the field becomes a nullable non-key UUID).

The full FRG-2NN matrix and worked examples for every code introduced in 0.6.0 Welding live in Compile-time diagnostics. This page keeps the FRG-215 details inline because the Troubleshooting section needs to stand alone for consumers reading ferra-forge.md in isolation.

Class 5 — not a struct with named fields (FRG-005)

error: FRG-005: FerraModel must be derived on a struct with named fields (not tuple structs, unit structs, enums, or unions)
         help: change the item to `pub struct <Name> { <named fields> }`
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-005

Fix. Convert to pub struct Name { ... } with named fields.

Class 6 — generic struct (FRG-006)

error: FRG-006: FerraModel does not currently support generic models
         help: supply a concrete type — remove the generic parameter
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-006

Class 7 — lifetime-parameterised struct (FRG-007)

error: FRG-007: FerraModel does not currently support lifetime-parameterised models
         help: Ferra models are owned values — remove the lifetime parameter
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-007

Class 8 — visibility below pub(crate) (FRG-008)

error: FRG-008: FerraModel requires at least `pub(crate)` visibility
         help: widen the struct's visibility — e.g., `pub struct ...` or `pub(crate) struct ...`
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-008

Class 9a — unknown #[ferra(...)] key, no nearest match (FRG-009)

error: FRG-009: `#[ferra(<key>)]` is not a recognized attribute
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-009

Fix. Consult the Recognised keys table above, or the Deferred keys table if you were trying to use a future-phase key.

Class 9b — unknown #[ferra(...)] key with a near-miss hint (release-blocker family; FRG-009, and FRG-308 for writeonly)

error: FRG-308: `#[ferra(writeonly)]` is not a recognized attribute
         help: did you mean `write_only`?
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-308

Fix. The help line quotes the intended spelling. The canonical case is #[ferra(writeonly)] on password_hash — a write-only bypass that would expose sensitive data. The trybuild fixture for this diagnostic is marked a release blocker per SC-008.

Class 10 — read_only + write_only contradiction (FRG-302)

error: FRG-302: `#[ferra(read_only)]` and `#[ferra(write_only)]` contradict
         help: keep at most one of the two flags
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-302

Class 11 — #[ferra(required)] on Option<T> (FRG-011)

error: FRG-011: `#[ferra(required)]` contradicts `Option<T>`
         help: write `#[field(required)]`: `required` is a `#[field(...)]` key; or remove it
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-011

Fix. required is a #[field(...)] key, never a #[ferra(...)] one: write #[field(required)], or remove the attribute. Nullability itself is deduced from the type.

Class 12 — #[ferra(write_only)] on the primary key (FRG-304)

error: FRG-304: primary key column `id` cannot be `#[ferra(write_only)]`
         help: remove `#[ferra(write_only)]` from the primary-key field
         note: primary keys must round-trip through `_links.self.href` and PK-path URL segments — a write-only PK cannot be reconstructed; see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-304

Class 13 — empty #[ferra(resource = "")] (FRG-013)

error: FRG-013: `#[ferra(resource)]` must be a non-empty string
         help: remove the attribute to fall back to the default
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-013

Class 14 — non-string-literal #[ferra(resource = ...)] (FRG-014)

error: FRG-014: `#[ferra(resource)]` value must be a string literal
         help: e.g., `#[ferra(resource = "films")]`
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-014

Class 15 — missing serde derives (no FRG code: FRG-015 is intentionally unallocated)

Delivered by rustc E0277 on the emitted _assert_ferra_model_bounds trait-bound assertion (see § Explicit serde derives are required above). Span is pinned to your struct’s identifier.

Class 16 — missing DeriveEntityModel sibling (FRG-016)

error: FRG-016: FerraModel requires DeriveEntityModel on the same struct
         help: add DeriveEntityModel to the `#[derive(...)]` list
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-016

Fix. Add DeriveEntityModel to the #[derive(...)] list. See the Canonical entity shape example above.

Degraded diagnostic under one specific shape. The Ferra-authored class-16 message above fires when the struct has zero #[sea_orm(...)] attributes (neither at container level nor on fields). If you forget DeriveEntityModel but do keep a #[sea_orm(primary_key)] on a field, rustc errors earlier than ferra-forge runs with cannot find attribute sea_orm in this scope — the sea_orm helper is unregistered without its owning derive. As a final safety net for any remaining edge case, the emitted code contains a `_assert_derives_entity_model<T:
:sea_orm::ModelTrait>()bound assertion; a failure there surfaces aserror[E0277]: the trait bound <YourModel>: sea_orm::ModelTrait is not satisfied. All three paths reduce to the same fix: add DeriveEntityModelto the#[derive(…)]` list.

Unknown #[sea_orm(...)] key (pass case)

An unknown-to-Ferra but Sea-ORM-permitted key such as #[sea_orm(column_name = "...")] compiles without intervention from Ferra. This is the asymmetry documented in § Two attribute namespaces, two policies. If Sea-ORM diagnoses the key itself, that diagnostic surfaces — Ferra does not layer its own.

Compile-time diagnostics — the FRG-NNN namespace

Which codes exist. The derive-shape codes (FRG-001 through FRG-023, with FRG-002, FRG-004, FRG-010, FRG-012 and FRG-015 intentionally unallocated), the validation-attribute codes (FRG-201 through FRG-215), the projection, computed and write-only codes (FRG-301 through FRG-326, with FRG-313 intentionally unallocated, and FRG-306 and FRG-330 through FRG-334 retired), the behavior codes (FRG-320 through FRG-323, and FRG-327), the collection-read codes (FRG-350 through FRG-358), the field-mode codes FRG-359 through FRG-365, the authorization codes (FRG-100 through FRG-152; #[operation(...)] is refused with FRG-335, groups with FRG-137, an attribute where the derive does not read it with FRG-138, and action(...) declarations with FRG-139 through FRG-146), the FerraLayer::base_path codes (FRG-340 through FRG-342) and the dependency code FRG-400.

Every example on this page is compiled. A bad example is a rust,compile_fail block, and the guide’s guide_blocks check compiles it and requires the compiler to say the code of its section, not just to fail; a good example is a plain rust block, compiled by cargo test --doc -p ferra-doc-playground. A section whose code cannot be raised by application code (retired, reserved, or guarding a type nobody outside Ferra can write) says so instead of showing an example. Where a section names a fixture, the fixture is the byte-for-byte contract of the message (.stderr).

Reader contract. This page stands on its own. A reader with only this page plus standard Rust and Sea-ORM knowledge can identify the trigger condition for any FRG-NNN error in the table below and fix the offending source on the first attempt. Cross-references to ADRs and the constitution are non-load-bearing — every correctness cue is spelled out in the per-code section.

#[derive(FerraModel)] and the #[field(...)] attribute parser emit typed FRG-NNN codes on every diagnostic. Each code is grep-friendly, span-anchored on the offending source token, and documented below with a worked-bad → worked-good example pair plus a one-sentence fix template.

ferra-forge collects independent diagnostics rather than stopping at the first mistake — multiple independent mistakes on the same struct surface in one cargo check round-trip. If any diagnostic is reported for a model, no code is generated for that model. The emitted shape carries three logical lines (error: + help: + note:) anchored to the offending token. The note: line points to the guide section that owns the rule: ferra-forge.md for most derive-shape codes, the page of the subject for a few (pagination.md, ferra-auth.md, ferra-core.md), this page for FRG-021, FRG-022 and FRG-023. FRG-018 has no note.

Namespace structure

FRG-000 .. FRG-099   derive-shape errors        (0.14.0 — FRG-001, FRG-003, FRG-005..FRG-009, FRG-011,
                                                 FRG-013, FRG-014, FRG-016..FRG-023; FRG-002, FRG-004,
                                                 FRG-010, FRG-012, FRG-015 intentionally unallocated)
FRG-100 .. FRG-199   authorization errors       (0.8.0, 0.9.0 — FRG-100..FRG-113, FRG-150, FRG-151; 0.10.0 — FRG-152;
                                                 0.13.0 — FRG-117..FRG-136; 0.14.0 — FRG-137..FRG-146, FRG-153;
                                                 FRG-105 retired)
FRG-200 .. FRG-299   validation-attribute       (0.6.0 Welding — FRG-201..FRG-215)
FRG-300 .. FRG-399   projection / computed /    (0.6.5 Chasing — FRG-301..FRG-316,
                     write-only attribute        FRG-313 intentionally unallocated,
                                                 FRG-306 and FRG-330..FRG-334 retired, FRG-335;
                                                 0.15.0 — FRG-359..FRG-362; 0.16.0 — FRG-363..FRG-365)
FRG-400 .. FRG-499   application dependencies     (0.9.0 — FRG-400)
FRG-500 ..           later phases               (reserved)

Code numbers are never recycled. A code retired because the class becomes unreachable remains documented as historical (see the FRG-215 note on Class 4 retirement); future codes append to the namespace.

How to read each entry

Every section below carries:

  • Trigger. A one-sentence description of when the error fires plus the offending #[field(...)] attribute pattern.
  • Bad. A short worked example showing the mistake. Paste it, with its hidden lines, into a sandbox crate to reproduce the diagnostic.
  • Good. A 5-15-line worked example showing the fix. Replaces the bad block one-for-one — same imports, same struct shape, only the offending attribute (or field type) changes.
  • Fix. A one- or two-sentence prescription naming what to change and where.
  • Fixture. A repo-relative link to the corresponding compile-fail fixture under crates/ferra-forge/tests/diagnostics/ (or, for the authorization codes, crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/). The fixture is the byte-shape contract — a CI-checked .stderr snapshot proves the diagnostic shape stays stable across releases.

Every example is a complete model and is compiled by the guide’s checks: a bad example (compile_fail) must fail with the code of its section, a good example must compile. What every example shares is hidden, in lines that start with # (the rendered book folds them away; on a raw page they are the first and last lines of each block):

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
// … the example …
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}                       // the Sea-ORM boilerplate
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

Every model declares a posture (#[ferra(auth = "none" | "bearer")] or an #[authorize] block, FRG-100), so that a bad example fails for its own reason and for no other. Paste a block, with its hidden lines, into a project that declares ferra, sea-orm, serde and tokio to reproduce the error.

Every model must also declare an authorization posture (see FRG-100). The authorization entries (FRG-1NN) show it; the other entries leave it out to stay short. When you reproduce one of them, add #[ferra(auth = "none")] under #[sea_orm(table_name = …)]; otherwise FRG-100 can fire next to the code you are studying, and the “Good” block does not compile.

FRG-0NN — derive-shape diagnostics (0.14.0)

The shape of the item the derive is written on, and the values of the keys of #[ferra(...)]. They come from #[derive(FerraModel)], which refuses to generate code for a model it cannot read. Until 0.14.0 these errors had no code. Each class of ferra-forge.md § Troubleshooting now has one: class N is FRG-0NN, except class 10 (FRG-302), class 12 (FRG-304) and the classes 2, 4 and 15, which have no FRG-0NN (below). FRG-017 to FRG-023 are new codes, for errors that had no class.

FRG-002, FRG-004, FRG-010, FRG-012 and FRG-015 are intentionally unallocated, like FRG-313: class 2 (composite primary keys) has been supported since 0.6.0, class 4 is historical (retired in 0.6.0, see the note on Class 4 under FRG-215), class 10 is FRG-302, class 12 is FRG-304, and class 15 is rustc’s E0277 on the serde bound. They have no section, and no number is ever recycled.

The examples declare auth = "none" so that FRG-100 does not fire beside the code being shown, and leave out the Sea-ORM boilerplate as everywhere on this page.

Trigger. No field of the model carries #[sea_orm(primary_key)]. Reported at the struct name.

#[ferra(auth = "none")]

    pub title: String,
}

FRG-018 — the Ferra facade is not a dependency

Trigger. #[derive(FerraModel)] finds neither ferra nor ferra-core in the [dependencies] of the crate it is expanded in (nor a dependency on ferra-rs, the other package name the facade is accepted under). The generated code names Ferra’s types, and cannot without one of them. Reported at the struct name. A model with an action(...) (or #[ferra(hooks)]) also needs ferra-http, directly or through the facade: when neither is there, the same error is reported at the first action key (at the hooks key for hooks), not at the struct name, and its last line names ferra-http; an action refused for another code shows that code instead. The message names no release tag: it would go stale at every release; the tag to write is the one of the release you use. The message names the derive that is expanded (#[derive(FerraModel)] here, #[derive(ActionBody)] for an action’s body type).

error: FRG-018: `#[derive(FerraModel)]` needs the Ferra facade: add it to your `[dependencies]` with the Git tag of the release you use, for example

           ferra = { git = "https://github.com/ferra-rs/ferra", tag = "<the release you use>" }

FRG-023 — an attribute that does not parse

Trigger. An attribute the derive reads is not written in the grammar it reads: a bare #[ferra] or #[field] (no parentheses), a key with no = (#[ferra(resource)]), projection with no parentheses, or a value that is not the expected token. The derive reads attributes with syn, the Rust parser crate, and syn says what it expected; the derive adds the code and keeps syn’s span, so the error points at the token syn stopped on: the attribute’s name for a missing argument list, the token after the key (often the closing parenthesis) for a missing =. A message that already carries a code is left as it is. #[authorize] is not in this class: the same mistakes in #[authorize] (a bare #[authorize], a key with no =) keep their code FRG-103, with syn’s message, as they always had.

error: FRG-023: the attribute does not parse: expected attribute arguments in parentheses: #[ferra(...)]
         help: write the attribute as the guide shows it: `name(...)` for a list, `name = value` for a key
         note: see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-023

FRG-1NN — authorization diagnostics (0.8.0, 0.9.0)

Every Ferra model declares who may do what. It does so with a posture (#[ferra(auth = "bearer")] — every operation needs a valid bearer token; #[ferra(auth = "none")] — deliberately public), with an #[authorize(...)] block that gives one rule per operation, or with both (the block then decides). A rule is built from five checkers — Anyone, Authenticated, IsOwner, IsAdmin, HasRole("role") — combined with + (all must pass), | (at least one passes) and parentheses. The operations are list, get, create, update, delete, plus restore on a model with #[behavior(soft_delete)].

The codes below fire when that declaration is missing, ambiguous, or would not be enforced. FRG-100 to FRG-113 come from #[derive(FerraModel)] and point at the model; FRG-150 and FRG-151 come from the Foundry mount call, FRG-152 from a handler that reaches a model’s rows. The full authorization guide is ferra-auth.md; each entry below stands on its own.

The Sea-ORM boilerplate (Relation enum, ActiveModelBehavior impl) is left out as everywhere on this page. Uuid comes from sea_orm::entity::prelude::*.

FRG-100 — model declares no authorization posture

Trigger. The struct carries neither #[ferra(auth = "...")] nor an #[authorize(...)] block. Ferra refuses to decide between a public and a protected model for you (deny by default). Reported at the struct name.

Bad.

    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

}

FRG-101 — #[authorize] is empty or incomplete

Trigger. One of three forms, all of which would leave an operation without a meaningful rule:

  • the block names some operations but not all of list, get, create, update, delete — the message lists the missing ones, and the error points at the struct name;
  • the block is empty: #[authorize()];
  • a HasRole names an empty or whitespace-only role: HasRole(""), HasRole(" ") — the error points at the string.

restore is optional and never reported missing: without a restore = … rule, restoring a soft-deleted row requires both the update and the delete rule to pass.

On a #[ferra(system_only)] model the block asks for list and get only: Ferra serves no write for it (see FRG-135).

FRG-101 also appears next to FRG-102 or FRG-103: a rule that fails to parse is dropped, so its operation then counts as missing. Fix the first error and the FRG-101 goes away with it.

Trigger. One predicate combines AND (+) and OR (|) without grouping, so it could be read two ways. Ferra does not assume a precedence. The error points at the predicate; FRG-101 follows for the same operation (see FRG-101).

FRG-103 — unknown, qualified or malformed checker

Trigger. A predicate is not built from the closed vocabulary:

  • a name outside Anyone, Authenticated, IsOwner, IsAdmin, HasRole — a typo such as IsOwnr is refused, never treated as a pass-through;
  • a checker written as a path, such as AuthRule::IsAdmin — the vocabulary is spelled bare, and the help names the bare form;
  • HasRole without exactly one string-literal argument (HasRole, HasRole(editor), HasRole("a", "b")), or an operator other than + and |;
  • an #[authorize] that does not parse at all (a bare #[authorize], a key with no =): syn’s message after the code, at the token syn stopped on. This is a grammar error, not a checker, and the code is misleading; it is kept as it has always been, not folded into FRG-023.

Each offending predicate is reported where it is written. When some rules still parse, FRG-101 follows for the dropped ones (see FRG-101).

FRG-104 — unknown, duplicated or routeless operation

Trigger. One of three forms, each reported at the operation key:

  • a key other than list, get, create, update, delete, restore (read = …, patch = …);
  • the same key twice in the block;
  • restore = … on a model without #[behavior(soft_delete)]: such a model has no restore route, so the rule would govern nothing.

FRG-105 — authorize on a projection (removed in 0.9.0)

Retired in 0.13.0. From 0.9.0 to 0.12.x, #[ferra(projection(..., authorize = ...))] was refused with this code: the key used to compile and enforce nothing, so a projection’s routes stayed open. Since 0.13.0 a projection’s authorize is parsed, enforced and answered with a 404 for a caller it refuses, so the key is valid and this code is never raised. The section stays as history, and the number is never recycled. The new codes are FRG-117 (a projection that widens exposure must say who may use it) and FRG-118 (IsOwner is not a projection rule). If you see FRG-105, you are reading output from a Ferra release older than 0.13.0.

FRG-106 — exposure (removed in 0.9.0)

Trigger. #[ferra(exposure = "...")], whatever the value. The key used to let a model compile without a posture, and every value — "auto_read_only" included — mounted all routes, writes included, without authentication. Reported at the exposure key.

Bad.

#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[ferra(exposure = "auto_read_only")]

    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

FRG-114 — owner field on a model whose create admits an anonymous caller

Trigger. The model has a #[field(owner)] field and its create rule lets a caller without a token in: create = Anyone, an Anyone branch (Anyone | IsAdmin), or #[ferra(auth = "none")] without an #[authorize] block. Ferra writes the owner of a new row from the caller’s token; without a token there is no owner to write. Reported at the owner field. A #[ferra(system_only)] model is not checked: Ferra serves no create for it, so no anonymous caller can reach one.

FRG-116 — a serde attribute changes a JSON name or shape

Trigger. A #[serde(...)] attribute that renames, hides, flattens or re-serializes a model field — on a field: rename, alias, flatten, skip, skip_serializing, skip_deserializing, skip_serializing_if, serialize_with, deserialize_with, with, getter; on the model: rename_all, rename_all_fields, tag, transparent, from, try_from, into, remote — or a #[serde(...)] attribute Ferra cannot read. Ferra names fields by their Rust name in bodies, projections, filters, links, the owner check and OpenAPI; a renamed owner answered 404 to its own owner, a renamed field disappeared from responses. Reported at the attribute key, once per offending key.

The same attributes are refused on the struct and the fields of an action body (#[derive(ActionBody)], FRG-145 refuses its other serde attributes): a body is read by its Rust field names too. A body has no #[ferra(...)] attribute, so the help: for a body is not the model’s: rename the field itself; a body takes no #[serde] attribute.

FRG-117 — a projection widens exposure without authorize

Trigger. A projection’s read or write set holds a field the bare path does not expose or accept, and the projection declares neither authorize = <rule> nor authorize = inherit. The bare path is the projection promoted with default = true, or else the model’s own default read and write shapes. A projection that shows or accepts less than the bare path, or the same, needs nothing: it inherits the model’s rules, unless the projection promoted with default = true carries a restricting rule (see the second case below). Reported at the projection’s name, naming the projection and the field(s) it adds.

Second case: a sibling of a ruled default projection. The rule of a default = true projection binds the bare path only. When that rule restricts callers (anything but Anyone and inherit), every other projection of the model must declare its own authorize, whatever its fields and its prefix: without one, /brief/films would serve the same fields to every caller the model admits, the alternate path to what the bare path refuses (CWE-288). The message names the sibling, the model, the promoted projection and its rule; the help offers that rule, another rule, or authorize = inherit to open the sibling knowingly. A sibling that also widens gets this one diagnostic. A promoted projection with no rule, or with authorize = Anyone, asks nothing of its siblings.

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;

#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[ferra(projection(
    name = "public",
    default = true,
    promotes_from = "auto-derived",
    breaking_change_version = "0.13.0",
    read = [id, title],
    write = [title],
))]
#[ferra(projection(name = "admin", read = [id, title, cost], write = [title]))] // adds `cost`
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
    pub cost: f64,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Add authorize = <rule> to say who may use the projection’s routes. The rule is added to the model’s rule of each operation (both must pass), and a caller it refuses gets the same 404 as for a row that does not exist. If the model’s own rules are enough, say so with authorize = inherit. authorize = Anyone is accepted and has the effect of inherit; neither is checked for being a real restriction, and Authenticated on a bearer model is equally ineffective. Two projections of the same name are never merged (FRG-310), whichever carries an authorize.

A field with its own rule of the matching direction is exempt (0.13.0): a read rule exempts a field that widens the projection’s read set, a write rule one that widens its write set, because that field’s exposure is already decided per caller. A rule of the other direction exempts nothing, and neither does a rule that admits everyone (FRG-119).

Fixtures. frg_117_projection_widens_read_without_authorize.rs. The other cases (a write widening, a sibling of a ruled default, a write-only sibling, a widening sibling, a rule of the other direction) are the unit tests frg_117_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/parse.rs.

FRG-118 — IsOwner in a projection’s authorize

Trigger. IsOwner appears anywhere in the rule of a projection’s authorize. A projection rule is decided once per request, from the caller alone, before any row is read and before any statement; IsOwner compares the caller with a row’s owner, so it has nothing to compare. Reported at the IsOwner token.

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Put ownership in the model’s #[authorize(...)], which still applies under the projection’s prefix, and keep the projection rule to a role or Authenticated.

FRG-119 — a field rule that cannot take effect

Trigger. A #[field(read = <rule>)] or #[field(write = <rule>)] that no request can ever be judged by, or that gates nothing. Reported at the read / write key, naming the field and the reason (at the rule’s value for the last case of the list, blameable(read = IsOwner)):

  • read on a write_only or skip field, on the cursor key, on a primary-key column (cursor tokens and the self / Location hrefs carry the key; a read rule on the owner column is allowed), or on a field no read projection serves;
  • write on a read_only, computed or skip field, a primary-key column, the owner field, or a field no write projection accepts;
  • a rule that admits the anonymous caller: Anyone, or Anyone | X. It gates nothing. (Known limit: Authenticated on a bearer model is equally ineffective and is not detected.)
  • filterable or sortable beside a read rule that uses IsOwner: a per-row visibility cannot gate a SQL predicate.
  • IsOwner in #[behavior(blameable(read = ...))] (0.13.0): the blame columns are shown or hidden once per request, not per row. (read = Anyone is allowed there: when read is left out, blameable uses Authenticated, so only an authenticated caller sees the blame columns, and Anyone shows them to every caller.)

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "employees")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub name: String,
    #[ferra(skip)]
    #[field(read = HasRole("hr"))] // a skipped field is in no response
    pub salary: Option<i64>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

FRG-120 — IsOwner in a field’s write rule

Trigger. IsOwner anywhere in a field’s write rule. A write projection is shared by POST and PUT, so the rule is judged on a create too, where the row has no owner yet. Reported at the IsOwner token. (IsOwner is allowed in a read rule: it is judged per row, on the owner column already loaded.)

FRG-121 — a blameable model lets an anonymous caller write

Trigger. A model enrolls #[behavior(blameable)], which stamps the subject of the caller who wrote the row, and the resolved rule of an operation that writes it admits a caller with no identity: create and update, and on a soft-delete model delete and restore as well (they set updated_by), and each action(...) too, whose authorize rule is its own (it has no posture default). The resolved rule is the one in #[authorize(...)], or the posture’s when there is no block (auth = "none" is Anyone for every operation). Reported at the blameable name, listing the operations, an action as action `name` . A projection rule cannot loosen the model’s, so the model’s rules are what counts. A #[ferra(system_only)] model serves none of these writes, so the check does not apply to it.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[behavior(blameable)]
#[authorize(
    list = Authenticated,
    get = Authenticated,
    create = Anyone, // no caller, no author
    update = Authenticated,
    delete = Authenticated
)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

FRG-122 — a Ferra key on a relation field

Trigger. A #[field(..)], #[authorize(..)], #[behavior(..)], #[operation(..)] or #[ferra(..)] attribute on a HasMany<..>, HasOne<..> or BelongsTo<..> field of a model written with #[sea_orm::model]. A relation is not a column: no Ferra key applies to it yet, so the key would declare something that has no effect, and the derive refuses it rather than let it look like a rule. Reported at the key.

FRG-123 — owner(from) names no BelongsTo field

Trigger. #[field(owner(from = x))] where x is not a BelongsTo<..> field of the same model: it names no field, a plain column, a HasMany<..> or HasOne<..> field (the side that holds the children cannot reach a parent), or a string (the spelling of Sea-ORM’s own from = "column"). from names the relation field that points at the parent; the row is owned through that parent’s owner. Reported at the from value.

FRG-125 — a relation field outside the dense form

Trigger. A HasMany<..>, HasOne<..> or BelongsTo<..> field on a struct that #[derive(FerraModel)] cannot tell is an expansion of #[sea_orm::model]: the struct is neither the scalar Model that macro leaves (marked #[sea_orm(model_ex)]) nor its ModelEx. The derive refuses it rather than expand it to nothing. It also catches a future Sea-ORM that changes the shape of the expansion. Reported at the relation field’s name.

FRG-126 — an authority without a list condition

Trigger. A model declares #[ferra(authority)] and serves list (every complete rule set does: #[authorize(...)] names all five operations, and a model with no block serves list under its posture), and no impl FerraListAuthority for Model exists. Without a condition a list would show every row, whatever can says about each, so Ferra refuses to compile it rather than leave the list unfiltered. Reported at the authority key.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use ferra::authority::{AuthorityError, FerraAuthority};
use ferra::meta::Operation;
use ferra::request_context::RequestContext;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", authority)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub team_id: i64,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

impl FerraAuthority for Model {
    fn can(_ctx: &RequestContext, _op: Operation, row: &Self) -> Result<bool, AuthorityError> {
        Ok(row.team_id == 1)
    }
}
// no `impl FerraListAuthority for Model`
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use ferra::authority::{AuthorityError, FerraAuthority, FerraListAuthority};
use ferra::condition::Condition;
use ferra::meta::Operation;
use ferra::request_context::RequestContext;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", authority)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub team_id: i64,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

impl FerraAuthority for Model {
    fn can(_ctx: &RequestContext, _op: Operation, row: &Self) -> Result<bool, AuthorityError> {
        Ok(row.team_id == 1)
    }
}

impl FerraListAuthority for Model {
    fn filter(_ctx: &RequestContext) -> Result<Condition<Self>, AuthorityError> {
        Ok(Model::FIELDS.team_id.eq(1_i64))
    }
}
}

Fix. Implement FerraListAuthority for the model: its filter returns the rows the caller may list, as a Condition built from Model::FIELDS. Keep it equal to what can allows for get.

        #[field(owner(from = context))]
        pub owner_id: i32,
        #[sea_orm(belongs_to, from = "context_id", to = "id")]
        pub context: BelongsTo<super::context::Entity>,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}
fn main() {}

Fix. Add #[field(owner)] to the parent, with the type of this model’s owner field; or change this model’s owner field to the type the parent’s owner has.

Fixtures. frg_127_parent_without_owner.rs, frg_127_parent_owner_of_another_type.rs.

FRG-128 — the authority key without an authority

Trigger. A model declares #[ferra(authority)] and nobody wrote impl FerraAuthority for Model. The key says the application decides access with its own code; with no code there is nothing to run, and Ferra does not guess. Reported at the authority key. Every complete rule set serves list, so the compiler also reports FRG-126 for the same key: a model with no authority has no list condition either.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", authority)] // declared, and no `impl FerraAuthority`
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub team_id: i64,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use ferra::authority::{AuthorityError, FerraAuthority, FerraListAuthority};
use ferra::condition::Condition;
use ferra::meta::Operation;
use ferra::request_context::RequestContext;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", authority)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub team_id: i64,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

impl FerraAuthority for Model {
    fn can(_ctx: &RequestContext, _op: Operation, row: &Self) -> Result<bool, AuthorityError> {
        Ok(row.team_id == 1)
    }
}

impl FerraListAuthority for Model {
    fn filter(_ctx: &RequestContext) -> Result<Condition<Self>, AuthorityError> {
        Ok(Model::FIELDS.team_id.eq(1_i64))
    }
}
}

Fix. Write impl FerraAuthority for Model (and impl FerraListAuthority for Model), or remove #[ferra(authority)] if the declared rules are enough.

The reverse is E0119. An impl FerraAuthority for Model on a model without the key conflicts with the allow-everything implementation the derive writes for it (“conflicting implementations of trait FerraAuthority”). That is deliberate: the key is what the other checks read, so an authority cannot be added without it. Add #[ferra(authority)]. The fixture fail_authority_impl_without_key.rs pins the message.

Fixtures. frg_128_authority_without_impl.rs.

FRG-129 — hooks without an impl, or an impl without hooks

Trigger. The two halves of a model’s hooks disagree.

  • The model declares #[ferra(hooks)] and nobody wrote impl FerraHooks for Model. The key says the application runs its own code inside the write; with no code there is nothing to run, and Ferra does not guess. Reported at the hooks key.
  • The model has impl FerraHooks for Model and declares no #[ferra(hooks)]. The key is what the other checks read (the request context, the draft), so hooks cannot be added without it. Reported at the impl.

Both are the compiler’s E0277 with the FRG-129 message.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]

#[ferra(auth = "bearer", hooks)] // declared, and no `impl FerraHooks`
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use ferra::hooks::FerraHooks;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", hooks)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

// Every hook has a default that does nothing: name the ones you use.
impl FerraHooks for Model {}
}

Fix. Declared with no impl: write impl ferra::hooks::FerraHooks for Model and override the hooks you need, or remove #[ferra(hooks)]. An impl with no declaration: add #[ferra(hooks)] to the model, or remove the impl. What a hook may and may not do is in Hooks.

Fixtures. fail_frg_129_hooks_without_impl.rs, fail_frg_129_impl_without_key.rs.

FRG-130 — a system grant toward a model that cannot take it

Trigger. #[ferra(hooks(system = T))] declares the hooks’ one system grant, and T cannot be its target. The grant bypasses the caller’s authorization on T, so Ferra checks what it can about T before it compiles. Each case below is refused, reported at the path of T (at the second key for the last):

  • T is not marked #[ferra(system_only)]: without it, T keeps its write routes and rules, and anything could write the log around the grant.
  • T has no database-generated integer primary key: a client_pk, a Uuid or a composite key. “The latest row” is the highest key, which the database must choose in commit order.
  • T has owner(from): its parent check is the caller’s authorization on the parent, and a grant bypasses it.
  • T is the hooked model itself, whatever the spelling of the path (Model, self::Model): its hooks would append to the table they run on. A model with hooks cannot be system_only (FRG-135), so the model is never a valid target and the case is the first bullet’s: the compiler’s E0277, with the same code.
  • T is another model on the hooked model’s table (same schema and table name): the hooks would still append to the table they run on. T is a valid target, so the bound passes; the derive compares the two table names and fails the constant evaluation with this code (E0080), the only guard for this case.
  • A second system key: a model has one grant, shared by its hooks.

The first three, and the hooked model itself, are the compiler’s E0277, with the FRG-130 message, on a hidden trait that only a valid target has. The shared table is a constant-evaluation error (E0080) with the same code, underlined over the whole path of T:

error[E0080]: evaluation panicked: FRG-130: the target of `hooks(system = ...)` is mapped on this model's own table, so its hooks would append to the table they run on (see docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md, FRG-130)
  --> src/film.rs:33:41
   |
33 | #[ferra(auth = "bearer", hooks(system = audit_entry::Model))]
   |                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ evaluation of `_::_` failed here

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod audit_entry {

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "audit_entries")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")] // not `system_only`
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i64,
        pub action: String,
    }
    #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
    pub enum Relation {}
    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]

#[ferra(auth = "bearer", hooks(system = audit_entry::Model))]

FRG-131 — #[ferra(me)] without a unique owner

Trigger. #[ferra(me)] makes GET /me return the caller’s own row, found by comparing the caller with the model’s owner column. That only works when the owner identifies one row, so the model needs a root #[field(owner)] that is either #[sea_orm(unique)] or the single-column primary key. Each case below is refused, reported at the me key:

  • the model has no #[field(owner)];
  • its owner is owner(from = ..): it comes from a relation, not from a column of this table;
  • its owner is neither #[sea_orm(unique)] nor the primary key, or is one column of a composite primary key: two rows could belong to the same caller.

Ferra reads the #[sea_orm(unique)] attribute on the field. A unique index that only a migration declares is not seen: add the attribute as well. If two rows do share an owner at runtime, GET /me answers 500 and logs it. A #[ferra(me)] model also needs an identity, see FRG-151.

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "profiles")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", me)] // the owner below can match several rows
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[field(owner)]
    pub owner_id: Uuid,
    pub name: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

FRG-133 — a field rule on a field a write projection requires

Trigger. A read or write rule on a field that a write projection requires: its type is not Option<T>, or a #[field(required)] rule makes it required. A caller who may not read the field could never create (the missing-field 422 would name it, and break the byte-identity with an unknown key), and one who may not write it could not create either. Reported at the read / write key. There is no notion of a database default.

FRG-134 — a blameable grant target while an anonymous caller may write

Trigger. The target T of #[ferra(hooks(system = T))] is #[behavior(blameable)], and the hooked model lets an anonymous caller through the rule of its create, update, delete or restore: its #[authorize] block says so, or, without a block, auth = "none". So does an action (#[ferra(action(...))]) whose own authorize an anonymous caller passes (Anyone): an action writes the row. A grant’s insert is stamped with the subject of the caller, so an anonymous write would append an entry with no author, and a blameable column refuses that. The four writes are checked whether or not the model soft-deletes. Reported at the path of T; the compiler’s E0277, with the FRG-134 message.

FRG-135 — a write rule on a system_only model

Trigger. A model marked #[ferra(system_only)] declares a create, update, delete or restore rule in its #[authorize] block. Ferra serves none of the four for such a model: it registers no route and documents no operation, and a write through Resource<M> is refused like an operation without a rule (403 with an identity, 401 without). Only a system grant writes it. A rule for an operation that does not exist would look like a posture and do nothing, so it is refused. The block asks for list and get only (FRG-101). Reported at the rule’s key.

A field’s #[field(write = ...)] rule is refused the same way: the model has no write route to gate, and the system grant’s insert ignores field rules. Reported at the field’s write key.

#[ferra(hooks)] is refused the same way, since 0.14.0: hooks run on a write, the model serves none, and the grant inserts without the target’s hooks, so they never ran. Reported at the hooks key. A model that writes through a grant declares hooks(system = T) on the hooked model, not on T.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "audit_entries")]
#[ferra(system_only)]
#[authorize(list = Authenticated, get = Authenticated, create = Authenticated)] // `create` is not served
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i64,
    pub action: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

    #[field(write = HasRole("admin"))] // no write route to gate

The update, delete and restore rules are the unit tests frg_135_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/authorize.rs; the field rule is frg_135_write_rule_on_system_only_field, and hooks and hooks(system = ...) are frg_135_hooks_on_system_only and frg_135_hooks_system_on_system_only, of crates/ferra-forge/src/parse.rs.

FRG-136 — a relation target or an owner(from) parent that is not a Ferra model

Trigger. A relation field (BelongsTo, HasOne or HasMany) whose target Entity belongs to a model that does not derive FerraModel, or an owner(from = x) whose parent is such a model. Ferra reads the target’s metadata to build the relation and, for owner(from), to follow the chain to the parent’s owner, so the target must be a Ferra model. Reported at the relation field’s target type, and for owner(from) also at the from value. A parent that is not a model also draws FRG-127, which is true of it and needs no separate fix.

The refusal has a second site. When the derive stays quiet but the target is still no Ferra model (an entity whose metadata is written by hand, without the derive), .mount of the model that holds the relation refuses it with the same text, naming the target: the bound that carries it is Served, in ferra-http. The fix is the same.

Bad.

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod context {
    use super::*;

    #[sea_orm::model]
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, Serialize, Deserialize)] // no `FerraModel`
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "contexts")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

mod source {
    use super::*;

    #[sea_orm::model]
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "sources")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        pub context_id: i32,
        #[sea_orm(belongs_to, from = "context_id", to = "id")]
        pub context: BelongsTo<super::context::Entity>,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}
fn main() {}

FRG-137 — groups has no effect

Trigger. The key groups is written, whatever its value: groups = ["admin"], groups = [], a bare groups, groups = "admin". It is refused on a field (#[ferra(groups = …)]), inside projection(...) and on the struct. Reported at the groups key.

Ferra does not scope fields by group. Until 0.14.0 the key was read and then dropped, so a field declared with it, groups = [] included, was served on every read and accepted in the default write body: a field believed restricted was served to everyone. A declaration that reads as a restriction must restrict, or not compile. #[field(groups = …)] is not a #[field(...)] key and keeps FRG-213; the typo group = [...] is the unknown-key error of #[ferra(...)], with a did you mean groups?.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "users")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(groups = [])]
    pub password_hash: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "users")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(write_only)]
    pub password_hash: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Say who may see or write the field in the way Ferra does:

  • read = [...] and write = [...] on a projection choose the fields of a shape;
  • #[field(read = …)] and #[field(write = …)] put a rule on one field;
  • #[ferra(skip)] keeps a field out of every response and write body, and #[ferra(write_only)] accepts it on write and never serves it.

See Migrating from 0.13 to 0.14.

Fixtures. frg_137_field_nonempty.rs. The other placements and values (bare, empty, a string, in a projection, on the struct, beside skip) are the unit tests frg_137_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/ferra_attrs.rs.

FRG-138 — an attribute where Ferra does not read it

Trigger. A Ferra attribute is written where the derive does not read it: #[field(...)] on the struct, or #[authorize(...)], #[behavior(...)] or #[operation(...)] on a field. Reported at the attribute path, whatever the attribute holds. The same attribute under the dense form #[sea_orm::model] is refused the same way. Where each namespace goes: Three attribute namespaces.

The compiler accepts every helper attribute the derive declares on the struct and on each field, so before 0.14.0 a misplaced one compiled and did nothing. A struct-level #[field(owner)] looked like the ownership marker and marked no field: the rows stayed readable by everyone the model’s rules let through (OWASP API1 and API3). A declaration that reads as a protection must protect, or not compile. #[operation(...)] on a field gets this code, not FRG-335: on a field the first problem is the place.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "notes")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[field(owner)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub owner_id: i32,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "notes")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[field(owner)]
    pub owner_id: i32,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Move the attribute where it is read, or remove it:

  • #[field(...)] goes on the field it describes;
  • #[authorize(...)] and #[behavior(...)] go on the struct; a rule for one field is #[field(read = …, write = …)];
  • #[operation(...)] goes nowhere: add the route yourself with .route(...) (custom handlers).

See Migrating from 0.13 to 0.14.

Fixtures. frg_138_field_on_struct_dense.rs (the dense #[sea_orm::model] form, which needs the real macro). The plain struct and the field cases are the unit tests frg_138_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/parse.rs.

FRG-139 — an action name that is not allowed

Trigger. The name of an action(...) is not snake case, or is reserved. A name is [a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*: lower-case letters and digits, words joined by single underscores, starting with a letter (mark_seen, ack_all, retry2; not mark-seen, Ack, 1x, a__b, a_). The name becomes a path segment and an operationId, so nothing else is accepted. These nine names are reserved: list, get, create, update, patch, delete, restore, self and collection. Ferra serves the first seven itself, and self and collection are path segments that already mean something. Reported at the name.

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", action(name = "mark-seen", authorize = Authenticated, handler = mark_seen))]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

FRG-141 — an unknown or repeated key inside action(...)

Trigger. A key of action(...) that Ferra does not know. The keys are name, authorize, handler, body, writes and collection. action(...) declares who may do what to a row, so a typo of authorize must not pass for an action whose rule was never set. When a known key is within two edits of the one written, the help line says did you mean. A key given twice is refused too, reported at its second occurrence: the last value used to win, so authorize = IsAdmin, authorize = Anyone widened the rule without a word. Reported at the key.

FRG-142 — an action without name, authorize or handler

Trigger. An action(...) leaves out name, authorize or handler. An action has no default rule: it does not borrow the model’s update rule, nor its posture (auth = "none" makes the CRUD operations anonymous, and gives an action no rule), so an action without authorize would have none to check. One error per missing key. An empty or malformed authorize is not this code: it is FRG-101, FRG-102 or FRG-103. Reported at the action key.

FRG-145 — a type an action body cannot be

Trigger. #[derive(ActionBody)] on the typed body of an action (body = T in action(...), ADR-0080) that Ferra cannot judge by its own rules. One error per mistake, reported at the token it concerns:

  • the type is not a struct with named fields, or has a generic parameter;
  • a field whose type is not a scalar Ferra field type (a String, a number, a bool, a Uuid, a date or time, or an Option of one of them): a serde_json::Value, a nested struct, a Vec;
  • a #[field(...)] key that is not one of the eight validation keys min_length, max_length, min, max, pattern, email, url and required (owner, filterable, json, …);
  • a #[serde(...)] attribute on the struct or on a field, other than those FRG-116 refuses on an action body as on a model: default, deny_unknown_fields, …

The keys Ferra checks, the values it validates and the schema it publishes are one list, the body’s own fields under their Rust names, so that the value the handler receives is the value that was checked: a body holds no nested object, no JSON value and no serde attribute.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::ActionBody;
use serde::Deserialize;
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct Detail {
    pub note: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize, ActionBody)]
pub struct ProgressBody {
    #[field(min = 0, max = 100)]
    pub progress: i32,
    pub detail: Detail,
}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::ActionBody;
use serde::Deserialize;
#[derive(Deserialize, ActionBody)]
pub struct ProgressBody {
    #[field(min = 0, max = 100)]
    pub progress: i32,
    #[field(max_length = 200)]
    pub note: Option<String>,
}
}

Fix. Flatten a nested object into scalar fields; give a field a type from the list above; keep to the eight validation keys; remove the #[serde(...)] attribute. For a value the caller may leave out, declare the field Option<T> instead of #[serde(default)]: serde reads an absent key as None, and the handler applies the default. Ferra already answers 422 unknown_field to a key outside the body’s fields, so deny_unknown_fields adds nothing.

Fixtures. frg_145_json_value.rs, frg_145_nested_struct.rs, frg_145_unsupported_key.rs, frg_145_serde_default.rs, frg_145_serde_deny_unknown_fields.rs, frg_145_generic.rs, frg_145_not_a_struct.rs

FRG-146 — a field an action cannot write

Trigger. A name in writes = [..] of an action(...) that is no field of the model, or that is not a read_only field or a field with a write rule of the model, or that is the key, the owner, the foreign key behind owner(from = ..), a computed field, a skip field or a field a behavior adds (created_at of timestampable). writes opens a field that is closed to the caller, to the action alone (Declared actions): a field that is already writable needs no opening, the key, the owner and the computed fields (the only fields with no column, FRG-364) are Ferra’s. The message depends on the name: a name that is no field of the model (a typo) reads “no field x on the model M”; a field the action cannot write reads “the field x cannot be written by an action: “ followed by its reason, one per kind above. One error per name, reported at the name in the list.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "tickets")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", action(name = "close", authorize = Authenticated, handler = close, writes = [title]))]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
    #[ferra(read_only)]
    pub status: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use ferra::hooks::{HookError, HookTx};
use ferra::request_context::RequestContext;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "tickets")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer", action(name = "close", authorize = Authenticated, handler = close, writes = [status]))]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
    #[ferra(read_only)]
    pub status: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
async fn close(
    mut row: Model,
    _ctx: &RequestContext,
    _tx: &mut HookTx<'_, Model>,
) -> Result<Model, HookError> {
    row.status = "closed".to_owned();
    Ok(row)
}
}

Messages. The first form is for a name that is no field of the model; the second for a field the action cannot write, its reason after the colon.

error: FRG-146: no field `statuss` on the model `Model`
         help: list the name of a `read_only` field or of a field with a `write` rule; check the spelling

error: FRG-146: the field `id` cannot be written by an action: it is the primary key; Ferra sets it
         help: remove it from `writes`; list only a `read_only` field or a field with a `write` rule

The reasons: “it is the primary key; Ferra sets it”, “it is the owner; Ferra sets it”, “it is the foreign key owner(from = ..) follows to the parent; moving it would hand the row to another owner” (when it is read_only or has a write rule: a foreign key that any caller may write gets the last reason), “it is computed; Ferra derives its value”, “it is skip: the API never reads or writes it”, “a behavior adds it; Ferra stamps it”, and “any caller who may write the row can already write it; writes opens only a closed field”.

Fix. List only a read_only field or a field with a write rule. Remove a field that any caller who may write the row can already write, and the key, the owner, the owner(from) foreign key, a computed field, a skip field and a field a behavior adds: an action cannot set them, listed or not. Check the spelling of a name the model does not have.

Fixtures. frg_146_free_field.rs, frg_146_key.rs, frg_146_owner.rs, frg_146_owner_from_fk.rs (the foreign key left writable: the reason of a free field), fail_action_writes_owner_from_fk_read_only.rs (the foreign key read_only: its own reason), frg_146_computed.rs, frg_146_skip.rs, frg_146_behavior_field.rs, frg_146_unknown_name.rs

FRG-150 — mounting a model without posture

Trigger. Two sites share this code.

  • Compile time, at Foundry::mount::<M>() (and mount_and_handle, mount_with_layer): M does not implement the marker trait FerraAuthConfigured. #[derive(FerraModel)] implements it for every model that declares a posture, and stops a model without one earlier, at FRG-100 — so only a hand-written FerraModel impl reaches this error.
  • Run time, in Foundry::build(): a mounted model leaves one of the operations it serves without a rule. build() panics and the server does not start. Only a hand-written ModelMeta (or a hand-written FerraAuthConfigured impl) can get there.
error[E0277]: FRG-150: `Film` has no declared authorization posture, but `Foundry::mount::<Film>()` requires one — deny by default

thread 'main' panicked at …:
FRG-150: the model `Film` has no authorization rule for the `list` operation — Ferra refuses to serve an operation it cannot authorize (deny by default). …

No example. The compile-time site needs a type that implements FerraModel by hand without implementing FerraAuthConfigured; the constructors of the model description (ModelMeta, FieldMeta) are #[doc(hidden)] in 0.9.0, so an application cannot write one, and the run-time site needs a hand-written ModelMeta too. The code is defense in depth behind FRG-100: #[derive(FerraModel)] stops a model without a posture before it reaches Foundry::mount. The fixture pins the message with a stand-in type.

What mounting a model with a posture looks like:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")] // or "bearer", or an `#[authorize(...)]` block
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let app = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).etag_key(std::env::var("ETAG_KEY")?)?.mount::<Model>().build();
Ok(())
}
}

Fix. Derive FerraModel and declare a posture on the model (see FRG-100). Do not implement FerraAuthConfigured by hand: it is a declaration that the model has a rule for every operation, and build() checks it.

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_mount_without_auth_configured.rs (compile time). The run-time panic is covered by the unit tests of crates/ferra-http/src/foundry.rs and crates/ferra-http/src/policy.rs.

FRG-151 — mounting without .with_auth() a model that needs an identity

Trigger. .mount::<M>() on a Foundry chain that has no .with_auth::<YourClaims>(jwt), where some rule of M needs an identity. With an #[authorize] block, that is any rule naming a checker other than Anyone; without a block, that is #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]. A projection’s authorize and a field’s read or write rule count too (0.13.0): a public model (auth = "none") with a projection or a field asking for Authenticated or a role needs .with_auth() as well. So does an action (#[ferra(action(...))]) whose own authorize names a checker other than Anyone, whatever the model’s rules say. So does a #[ferra(me)] model, whatever its rules say: GET /me compares the caller with the owner, so the model needs an identity (a FRG-131 model has a unique owner for it). Such a model could never authorize a caller: without a JWT configuration nothing turns a token into an identity. The error points at the mount call:

error[E0277]: FRG-151: `Film` requires an identity, but this `Foundry` chain has no `.with_auth()`
   |     let app = Foundry::new(conn).mount::<Film>().build();
   |                                  ^^^^^ `Film` cannot be mounted without a JWT configuration
   = help: the trait `AuthGate<Film>` is not implemented for `NoAuth`

Bad.

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
