Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
use ferra::{ClaimCheck, FerraIdentity, HmacAlgorithm, JwtConfig};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct MyClaims { sub: String }
impl FerraIdentity for MyClaims {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.sub }
    fn has_role(&self, _role: &str) -> bool { false }
}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let jwt = JwtConfig::single_secret(
    "key-1",
    std::env::var("JWT_SECRET")?,
    HmacAlgorithm::Hs256,
    ClaimCheck::expect("https://auth.example.com/"),
    ClaimCheck::expect("films-api"),
)?;
let app = ferra::Foundry::new(conn)
    .etag_key(std::env::var("ETAG_KEY")?)?
    .with_auth::<MyClaims>(jwt) // MyClaims: FerraIdentity + Deserialize
    .mount::<Model>()
    .build();
Ok(())
}
}

.mount_and_handle::<M>() has the same gate, so the same error:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) {
let (foundry, films) = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).mount_and_handle::<Model>(); // no `.with_auth()`
}
}

Fix. Call .with_auth::<YourClaims>(jwt) on the chain before the first .mount (it is not available once a model is mounted; before or after .api_version("v1")? makes no difference). If the model is deliberately public, declare #[ferra(auth = "none")] or make every rule Anyone instead — such a model mounts on any chain. ClaimCheck, JwtConfig and HmacAlgorithm are imported from ferra (they are not in ferra::prelude).

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_sec_004_bearer_without_with_auth.rs, and fail_mount_and_handle_without_auth.rs for mount_and_handle; fail_action_rule_without_with_auth.rs is a model whose only rule that needs an identity is an action’s.

FRG-152 — a route of your own without the resource handle

Trigger. A handler takes Resource<M> but the router state it runs on holds no ResourceHandle<M>: the handle was never issued (the model was mounted with .mount::<M>(), or not mounted), or it was not put in the state. The handle is how a route reaches the rows of a model under the model’s rules; only .mount_and_handle::<M>() issues one. The error points at the Resource<M> argument of the handler. Add #[axum::debug_handler] to the handler to get it (it needs axum with its macros feature): without it axum reports its own, opaque, “the trait Handler<…> is not implemented”, and says so.

error[E0277]: FRG-152: `()` carries no `ResourceHandle<Film>`
   |     async fn mine(_films: Resource<Film>) {}
   |                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ no handle for `Film` in this state
   = note: mount `Film` with `.mount_and_handle::<Film>()` and keep the handle in your router state (a field of your state that derives `FromRef`).

Bad.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
#[axum::debug_handler(state = ())]
async fn mine(_films: ferra::Resource<Model>) {}
fn demo() {
let _app: axum::Router = axum::Router::new()
    .route("/films", axum::routing::get(mine))
    .with_state(()); // the state holds no `ResourceHandle<Model>`
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
#[axum::debug_handler(state = ferra::ResourceHandle<Model>)]
async fn mine(_films: ferra::Resource<Model>) {}
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let (foundry, films) = ferra::Foundry::new(conn).etag_key(std::env::var("ETAG_KEY")?)?.mount_and_handle::<Model>();
let _app: axum::Router = foundry
    .build()
    .merge(axum::Router::new().route("/films", axum::routing::get(mine)).with_state(films));
Ok(())
}

Fix. Mount the model with .mount_and_handle::<M>() instead of .mount::<M>(), and keep the handle it returns in the state of the router the handler is on: .with_state(handle) for a router of one model, or a field of your own state that derives axum::extract::FromRef.

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_resource_handle_missing.rs

FRG-153 — an OpenAPI name produced twice

Trigger. Foundry::build() finds an OpenAPI component name or operationId that the mounted models register twice, and panics: the server does not start. The document keys its schemas by name, so the second registration would overwrite the first without a word, and a client generated from the document would read a model, or a projection, through the shape of another. Both registrations can come from

  • one model: a projection x-collection, whose read schema has the name of the list envelope of a projection x (FilmXCollection), or a projection collection-hal, whose read schema has the name of the HAL form of the default list envelope (FilmCollectionHal);
  • two models: Film with a summary projection, and a model FilmSummary (FilmSummary, CreateFilmSummaryInput, getFilmSummary);
  • a row action and another operation: the operationId of an action is its name in lowerCamel case and the model’s name (ack on Job is ackJob), so an action get_ack of a model Job produces getAckJob, the get of a model AckJob; an action patch_ack produces patchAckJob, its patch; an action a_b of Job and an action a of BJob both produce aBJob; two actions of one model whose names differ by an underscore before a digit (a_1 and a1) both produce a1Job. The body component of an action is a name too: it is the action’s name in PascalCase, the model’s name and Input (progress on Job is ProgressJobInput), so an action patch_x of Job with a body produces PatchXJobInput, the patch input of a model XJob, and an action ack with a body produces AckJobInput, the read schema of a model AckJobInput (an action cannot be called patch: the name is reserved, FRG-139);
  • a projection and the shared error schema: a projection details of a model Problem produces ProblemDetails, the schema every error response references.

A projection’s schemas are {Model} then the PascalCase of its name, with the Create…Input, Update…Input, Patch…Input, …Collection and …Hal forms. collection and hal are refused at compile time (FRG-317); this code covers every other pair of names, ProblemDetails included: Ferra registers it first, and a model or projection that produces it is the second owner.

Detection site. Foundry::build() reads the names where the document registers them, so it needs no .with_docs(). The operationIds are read in the whole document built, whatever the operation: CRUD, restore, /me, a row action’s, a projection’s.

The application refuses to start: Foundry::build() panics, before any route is served, with a one-line message about the first name it finds twice. The line below is that panic for the FilmXCollection example above (x and x-collection of the model Film).

FRG-153: the OpenAPI component `FilmXCollection` is produced twice, by projection `x` of the model `Film` and by projection `x-collection` of the model `Film`: the document would keep one and drop the other. Rename a projection (`#[ferra(projection(name = ...))]`), an action (`#[ferra(action(name = ...))]`) or a model's resource (`#[ferra(resource = ...)]`) so that the names differ. See docs/user-guide/ferra-forge-diagnostics.md § FRG-153.

The same refusal covers a patch_ack action against the patch of AckJob (patchAckJob, PATCH), two actions of two models (a_b of Job and a of BJob are both aBJob) and two actions of one model (a_1 and a1, both a1Job: the underscore before a digit is dropped).

FRG-213 — unknown #[field(...)] key

Trigger. A #[field(<key>)] invocation whose <key> is not in the closed #[field(...)] vocabulary. The closed vocabulary is the eight rules listed in ferra-forge.md § Validation rules — min_length, max_length, min, max, pattern, email, url, required. When the unknown key’s Levenshtein distance to a recognised key is ≤ 2, the diagnostic carries a did you mean <closest>? help line.

Trigger. A field declared as #[sea_orm(primary_key)] pub id: Option<Uuid> (or Option<Id>). Option<Uuid> was admitted as a field type in 0.6.0 Welding (User Story 4), but a primary key cannot be optional — an inserted None would be indistinguishable from a row whose key was never assigned, so the round-trip equality semantics a PK guarantees cannot hold.

Fix. Either drop the Option<...> from the field type (so the PK is always present) or remove #[sea_orm(primary_key)] from the tag (so the field becomes a nullable non-key UUID).

Note on Class 4. Option<Uuid> was previously rejected outright by #[derive(FerraModel)] (Class 4 in ferra-forge.md § Troubleshooting). 0.6.0 Welding lifts the rejection — the type is now first-class — and replaces it with this narrower contradiction check. If you came here looking for the old “Option<Uuid> is not supported” diagnostic, that class is retired; the per-rule rejection above is the current diagnostic.

Compile-time diagnostic wrappers

Some Ferra attributes impose a trait bound on the field’s type — for example, #[ferra(computed)] requires the field’s type to implement Default (Sea-ORM builds the #[sea_orm(ignore)] field with T::default()). When the bound is violated, rustc’s default message would be the language-level error[E0277]: the trait bound \T: Default` is not satisfied`. That phrasing is correct but tells the user nothing about why Ferra needs the bound or how to satisfy it in the Ferra-specific context.

To close that gap, ferra-core ships a small set of wrapper traits in ferra_core::diagnostics that re-export the underlying language traits under a framework-authored name and carry a #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented] annotation. The compiler reads the annotation and renders the framework’s message / label / note triple instead of its default E0277 text. The user sees a Ferra-shaped diagnostic on the first line of compiler output.

The shipped wrappers

Wrapper traitWrapped language traitConsumed by
FerraComputedDefaultDefault (blanket-impl’d for T: Default)ferra-forge’s compute_emit::emit_computed_bounds, once per #[ferra(computed)] field.
FerraSendSend (blanket-impl’d for T: Send + ?Sized)ferra-forge’s emit_bounds_assertion, once per field of the model, spanned at the field’s type. Ferra’s message appears when the field’s type is itself not Send (Rc<T>); for a struct that contains one, rustc names the inner type. Only a #[ferra(computed)] field can carry a type of yours: the classifier refuses any other type it does not know.
FerraSyncSync (blanket-impl’d for T: Sync + ?Sized)Sibling of FerraSend on the same per-field assertion (Cell<T> is Send and not Sync). Fixture: crates/ferra-forge/tests/ui/fail_non_sync_field.rs.
FerraComputednone — the trait itself carries the messageThe derive’s Model: FerraComputed assertion on the first computed field of a model (FRG-362).
FerraAuthConfigurednone — a marker with no blanket implFoundry::mount::<M>() (FRG-150). #[derive(FerraModel)] implements it for every model that declares a posture.
FerraMountableWithoutAuthnone — a marker with no blanket implFoundry::mount::<M>() on a chain without .with_auth(), through the AuthGate<M> bound (FRG-151). #[derive(FerraModel)] implements it for a model none of whose rules needs an identity and that is not #[ferra(me)].

FerraComputedDefault, FerraSend and FerraSync wrap a language trait. FerraAuthConfigured and FerraMountableWithoutAuth wrap nothing: they are markers the derive writes for you, and the only fix for a missing one is on the model (or on the Foundry chain), never a hand-written impl. The two authorization markers are documented under FRG-150 and FRG-151. HoldsResource, the sealed trait behind FRG-152, is the same kind: a bound with a message, and nothing to implement.

The canonical diagnostic shape

The compiler renders a #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented] failure as three lines anchored on the offending type. The message is the top-line error: …; the label is the inline span annotation pointing at the offending position; the note is the bottom-line fix hint. For FerraComputedDefault:

error[E0277]: `NotDefault` is used as the type of a `#[ferra(computed)]` field, but it does not implement `Default`
  --> src/model.rs:LL:CC
   |
LL |     pub total: NotDefault,
   |                ^^^^^^^^^^ this type needs `impl Default for NotDefault`
   |
   = note: A `#[ferra(computed)]` field's type must implement `Default`: add `#[derive(Default)]` to the type or write `impl Default` for it. (...)

The framing — is used as the type of a \#[ferra(…)]` fieldplus theimpl Defaultsuggestion in thelabel— is how a consumer (human or AI) recognises a Ferra wrapper diagnostic versus a generic rustc message. Whenever you see one of these triples, thenote:line names the fix verbatim; apply it on the offending type and re-runcargo check`.

Migration when an upgrade introduces a new wrapper-trait bound

Future Ferra releases land additional bounds (e.g. FerraAuthConfigured at 0.8.0). When an upgrade triggers a previously-passing compile to fail with a new wrapper-trait diagnostic:

  1. Recognise the framing. The message line names a Ferra attribute or generation context (required for fields marked \#[ferra(…)]`, FRG-150: … has no declared authorization posture`, …) rather than a bare language trait.
  2. Read the note: line. It names the concrete fix — a missing #[derive(...)], a missing impl, or a missing attribute on the model.
  3. Apply the fix at the named site. The diagnostic’s --> path:LINE:COL anchor points at the exact source position; the wrapper-trait substrate guarantees the fix is local to the type or the model under the cursor.

The per-code FRG-3NN sections below cite individual diagnostics; the wrapper-trait substrate is shared by every emission that imposes a typed bound on user fields (the FerraComputedDefault consumer site is documented under FRG-3NN — computed/projection codes that share the wrapper substrate).

Computed-field default-value diagnostic

A #[ferra(computed)] field has no column: Sea-ORM builds it with T::default() when it reads the entity, and the application’s FerraComputed fills it afterwards — so the field’s type must implement Default. The proc-macro emits a bound assertion through the FerraComputedDefault wrapper trait (see Compile-time diagnostic wrappers) so the diagnostic surfaces the framework-authored triple instead of rustc’s generic E0277 text.

Bad — a user-named type that does not implement Default.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use ferra::compute::FerraComputed;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use sea_orm::DeriveValueType;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// A user-defined newtype that deliberately omits `#[derive(Default)]`.
/// Every other trait Ferra's substrate requires (`Clone`, `Debug`,
/// `PartialEq`, sea-orm's `ValueType` family via `DeriveValueType`,
/// serde derives) is in place — `Default` is the only missing piece.
#[derive(
    Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveValueType, Serialize, Deserialize,
)]
pub struct NotDefault(pub i64);

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[sea_orm(ignore)]
    #[ferra(computed)]
    pub custom: NotDefault,
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
impl FerraComputed for Model {}
}

The diagnostic the developer sees — the framework-authored FerraComputedDefault #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented] triple, pinned verbatim by the trybuild golden crates/ferra-forge/tests/ui/computed_default_missing.{rs,stderr}:

error[E0277]: `NotDefault` is used as the type of a `#[ferra(computed)]` field, but it does not implement `Default`
  --> src/model.rs:LL:CC
   |
LL |     pub custom: NotDefault,
   |                 ^^^^^^^^^^ this type needs `impl Default for NotDefault`
   |
   = note: A `#[ferra(computed)]` field's type must implement `Default`: add `#[derive(Default)]` to the type or write `impl Default` for it. A model with a computed field must also write an `impl FerraComputed` for itself (an empty one when nothing is overridden), or `Foundry::mount` does not compile; see `docs/user-guide/computed-fields.md`. Diagnostic emitted by `ferra_core::diagnostics::FerraComputedDefault`.
   = note: required for `NotDefault` to implement `FerraComputedDefault`
help: consider annotating `NotDefault` with `#[derive(Default)]`

Fix. Add #[derive(Default)] (or an explicit impl Default) on the field’s underlying type:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use sea_orm::DeriveValueType;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(
    Default, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveValueType, Serialize, Deserialize,
)]
pub struct NotDefault(pub i64);
}

The build now succeeds and the wrapper-trait bound is satisfied via the blanket impl impl<T: Default> FerraComputedDefault for T {} on [ferra_core::diagnostics::FerraComputedDefault].

FR-043 — non-computed fields are unaffected. A user-named field type that does NOT carry #[ferra(computed)] is rejected by the classifier cascade (type … is not supported by Ferra). The classifier widening that admits NotDefault above lives behind the #[ferra(computed)] gate by design; the negative control unit test frg_003_non_computed_user_named_rejected of crates/ferra-forge/src/classify.rs pins this invariant.

Multi-segment paths (module::MyType) are not admitted at 0.7.0. Only single-ident user-named types pass the gate. A path-qualified type continues to be rejected by the classifier cascade even under the computed gate. Use a use module::MyType as MyType; at the declaration site to surface the bare ident if the wrapper-trait diagnostic is desired.

FRG-3NN — projection-attribute diagnostics (0.6.5 Chasing)

The 0.6.5 Chasing release opens the FRG-3NN block for projection / computed / write-only attribute rejections. Codes FRG-301..FRG-312 and FRG-314 ship from the proc-macro parser (#[derive(FerraModel)]); code FRG-312 is runtime-detected at Foundry::build() (cross-model collision check). FRG-315 is reserved and never emitted: the sub-collection is served at the bare path and no nested path takes a prefix (ADR-0030 as amended). FRG-313 is intentionally unallocated — the slot is reserved for namespace stability; the framework will not recycle the identifier.

See Projections and routing for the user-facing contract; this page documents the compile-time enforcement.

FRG-301 — projection references an unknown field

Trigger. A #[ferra(projection(... read = [...]))] or write = [...] list contains an ident that does not match any field on the host struct. The check also fires when an ident references a field but in the wrong half (e.g. a #[ferra(write_only)] field listed in a read = [...]; see FRG-305 for that refinement).

On a model written with #[sea_orm::model], a read list also accepts the name of a BelongsTo relation field: it is not unknown, it is an embed (Embedding). The name of a HasMany or a HasOne is FRG-363. Any other name that is no field is still unknown here.

FRG-302 — write_only and read_only on the same field

Trigger. A field carries both #[ferra(write_only)] and #[ferra(read_only)]. The two flags are mutually exclusive: a write-only field is inbound-only (e.g. a password on registration), a read-only field is outbound-only (e.g. a server-set timestamp); combining them produces a field that can be neither read nor written — a field nobody can interact with. Diagnostic span on the second-encountered flag.

FRG-303 — write_only and computed on the same field

Trigger. A field carries both #[ferra(write_only)] and #[ferra(computed)]. A computed field is server-produced — its value materialises at read time from other fields on the row — so it is strictly outbound. Tagging it write_only makes the field unreachable: the framework would never produce it on the read side and would reject inbound values on the write side. Diagnostic span on write_only.

FRG-304 — write_only on a primary-key field

Trigger. #[ferra(write_only)] on a field that also carries #[sea_orm(primary_key)]. Primary-key columns surface in _links.self.href and as /{resource}/{id} URL segments — they must round-trip on the read side. A write-only PK column would leave the inserted row structurally unaddressable. Composite-key models fire FRG-304 independently per PK column, so the developer resolves the full graph in one round-trip.

FRG-305 — write_only field appears in a read projection

Trigger. A field declared #[ferra(write_only)] is listed in some projection’s read = [...]. The structural exclusion of write-only fields from the read shape is the load-bearing security guarantee of US3 — there is no escape hatch via the projection attribute, even on an admin-scoped projection. Diagnostic span on the offending ident inside the read list.

FRG-306 — skip and non-empty groups on the same field

Retired in 0.14.0. From 0.6.5 to 0.13.x, a field that carried both #[ferra(skip)] and a non-empty #[ferra(groups = ["..."])] was refused with this code. groups never worked: the derive parsed it and dropped it, so a field with groups alone was served on every read and accepted in the default write body, as if the attribute were absent. Since 0.14.0 the key groups is refused whatever its value, so this code is never raised. The section stays as history, and the number is never recycled. The code that replaces it is FRG-137. To hide a field, use #[ferra(skip)] or #[ferra(write_only)]; to serve it only to some callers, name it in a projection’s read/write lists or give it a #[field(read = ...)] rule. If you see FRG-306, you are reading output from a Ferra release older than 0.14.0.

FRG-307 — legacy #[field(write_only)] form

Trigger. A field carries #[field(write_only)]. The #[field(...)] namespace is reserved for validation rules (FRG-201..FRG-215); write_only is a projection flag that lives under the #[ferra(...)] namespace per ADR-0006’s namespace harmonisation. The parser recognises the pre-ADR-0006 legacy spelling and emits FRG-307 with help pointing at the canonical #[ferra(write_only)] spelling.

FRG-309 — computed and read_only redundant

Trigger. A field carries both #[ferra(computed)] and #[ferra(read_only)]. The first attribute implies the second by construction — a computed field is server-produced and therefore appears only on the read shape — so the explicit read_only is redundant. Diagnostic span on the second-encountered flag with help suggesting the redundant attribute be dropped.

FRG-310 — projection URL prefix collision

Trigger. Two projections on the same model produce the same URL prefix. Two failure shapes share this code:

  • Duplicate path_prefix. Two projections each declare the same literal path_prefix = "...", so both route to the same URL.
  • Double default = true. Two projections each carry default = true; both target the bare resource path (/{resource}/{id}) and therefore collide. The second default = true is the offending span.

The proc-macro detects single-model collisions at compile time; the framework’s Foundry::build() startup pass covers cross-model collisions as defense-in-depth (see FRG-312 for the projection-vs-resource case).

Bad (duplicate path_prefix).

use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[ferra(projection(name = "admin",   path_prefix = "/staff", read = [id, title]))]
#[ferra(projection(name = "manager", path_prefix = "/staff", read = [id, title]))]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

FRG-311 — projection name is not a URL-safe segment

Trigger. A projection’s name = "..." cannot be normalised to a URL-safe segment (it contains characters outside [a-z0-9_-] after to_lowercase()) AND the projection does not supply an explicit path_prefix = "..." override. The framework needs a URL-safe segment to route the projection; when the name cannot produce one, the developer must either rename the projection or supply a path prefix verbatim.

FRG-312 — projection prefix collides with a resource route

Trigger. A projection’s auto-derived URL prefix collides with an existing resource route mounted elsewhere on the same Foundry. For example: model A is mounted at /admin, and model B declares a projection named admin — the projection would shadow the top-level resource at the shared URL prefix.

Detection site. This collision spans two models, so the proc-macro cannot see it at compile time (it parses one struct at a time). Detection lives at Foundry::build(): the runtime walks every registered resource route plus every projection prefix and panics on overlap with a FRG-312 error. The proc-macro emits no hint for this code.

Status at 0.6.5. The runtime collision check ships with the projection-routing wiring. A dedicated tests/diagnostics/frg_312_*.rs proc-macro fixture is intentionally absent — the diagnostic surface is runtime (a panic with the FRG-312 prefix), so the test lives as an integration assertion alongside other Foundry::build() checks rather than as a trybuild fixture.

Bad (compiles; panics when build() runs).

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod widget {
    use super::*;
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "widgets")]
    #[ferra(auth = "none")]
    #[ferra(projection(name = "admin", read = [id, title]))] // serves /admin
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        pub title: String,
    }
    #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
    pub enum Relation {}
    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

mod admin {
    use super::*;
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "admin")] // the resource is served at /admin too
    #[ferra(auth = "none")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        pub name: String,
    }
    #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
    pub enum Relation {}
    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let app = ferra::Foundry::new(conn)
    .etag_key(std::env::var("ETAG_KEY")?)?
    .mount::<widget::Model>()
    .mount::<admin::Model>() // panics: FRG-312
    .build();
Ok(())
}
fn main() {}

FRG-314 — write_only field omitted from an explicit write list

Trigger. A named projection declares an explicit write = [...] list that omits a #[ferra(write_only)] field on the host model. The default-write projection (auto-derived when write = [...] is omitted) already includes every write-only field by construction; this rejection only applies to projections that opt into an explicit list. The help suggests adding the missing field or removing the #[ferra(write_only)] declaration. Diagnostic span on the projection’s write key.

FRG-315 — reserved: no sub-resource takes a prefix

Status: reserved, never emitted. ADR-0030 once planned to reject a path_prefix on a model mounted as a sub-resource, because a nested path would take the root’s projection prefix. As amended (ADR-0084, 0.16.0), no nested path takes a prefix: a parent and its child serve only the sub-collection GET and POST {parent item}/{relation}, at the bare path and in the child’s default representation, and the child’s own path_prefix is its own (Nested resources). There is nothing to reject, so nothing raises this code. There is no example to compile, and no fixture. The number stays allocated.

FRG-316 — default = true requires promotes_from + breaking_change_version

Trigger. Three triggers, one code:

  • A projection declares default = true without both promotes_from = "..." and breaking_change_version = "..." attestations on the same declaration. Setting default = true replaces the bare-path response shape — a silent breaking change to the public API contract (consumers continue requesting /{resource}/{id} and receive a different schema). The two attestations force the change to be visible in the source. Reported at default = true.
  • A projection declares promotes_from without default = true (0.14.0). The attestation says what a promoted projection replaces; on any other projection it was read and dropped. Reported at the promotes_from key.
  • The value of promotes_from is neither "auto-derived" nor "named:<name>" with <name> another projection declared in the same model (0.14.0): "named:ghost" for a projection that does not exist, "v1" for a name written without named:, and the projection’s own name (a projection was not its own previous default). Reported at the value.

Why both are required. promotes_from names what is being replaced ("auto-derived" for the framework’s default, or "named:<other>" for a previous named-default projection). The macro checks the value against the projections the model declares, anywhere in the model, and never against repository history: a former named default that you removed in the same change can no longer be named (use "auto-derived"). breaking_change_version surfaces in the OpenAPI document as the x-ferra-promoted-in: "X.Y.Z" vendor extension on every operation under the bare resource path, so SDK consumers and downstream tooling can detect the silent break.

Nothing compares a model’s bare-path default with an earlier build: a lockfile that would record each model’s default and a hash of its schemas, and fail the build on a drift, is not planned. The two attributes above are the only protection, so a copied attestation that nobody re-read is not caught.

FRG-317 — a reserved projection name

Trigger. #[ferra(projection(name = "default", ...))], name = "collection" or name = "hal". default names the model’s own read and write shapes, served at the bare path. collection and hal are reserved since 0.14.0: a projection’s read schema in the OpenAPI document is {Model} then the PascalCase of its name, so they would overwrite the model’s own list envelope {Model}Collection and HAL read {Model}Hal. Reported at the name.

FRG-323 — a field has the name of a column a behavior owns

Trigger. The struct declares a field whose name, or whose #[sea_orm(column_name = "...")], is a column a behavior it enrolls in owns: deleted_at with #[behavior(soft_delete)], created_at or updated_at with #[behavior(timestampable)], created_by or updated_by with #[behavior(blameable)], or the names given in #[behavior(...)] (soft_delete(column = "removed_at"), blameable(updated_by = "editor")). The error is at the field and names the behavior column.

Why. Each enrolled behavior adds a field named after its column to the model’s metadata. A field of yours with that name, or stored in that column through #[sea_orm(column_name = "...")], would claim the same column a second time: the behavior and your struct would both own it. Ferra refuses it at the field, and the message says whether the clash is the Rust name or the column_name.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
    pub deleted_at: Option<String>, // the behavior adds this column itself
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)] // adds `deleted_at`
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. Remove the field: the behavior reads and writes that column itself, and the stamps and nothing else of it reach the clients. If you need a column of that name for something else, name the behavior’s column differently in #[behavior(...)]. If the clash is through column_name, change the field’s column_name instead, or the behavior’s column.

Fixture. crates/ferra-forge/tests/diagnostics/frg_323_behavior_field_conflict.rs (the span on the field’s identifier). The other clashes (a configured column, a blameable default or configured column, a #[sea_orm(column_name)]) point at the same token: the unit tests frg_323_* of crates/ferra-forge/src/parse.rs.

FRG-330 to FRG-334 — retired

These codes described the grammar of #[operation(path = ..., method = ...)]: a missing key, an unknown key, a / in the path, an unsupported method, a duplicate operation name. The attribute itself is refused since 0.9.0 (FRG-335), so none of them can fire any more. They are kept here as history and their numbers will not be reassigned. If you see one, you are reading output from a Ferra release older than 0.9.0.

FRG-330 — retired (missing #[operation] key)

See FRG-335.

FRG-331 — retired (unknown #[operation] key)

See FRG-335.

FRG-332 — retired (/ in #[operation(path)])

See FRG-335.

FRG-333 — retired (unsupported #[operation(method)])

See FRG-335.

FRG-334 — retired (duplicate operation name)

See FRG-335.

FRG-335 — #[operation(...)] is refused

Trigger. #[operation(...)] on a model, whatever its content. Before 0.9.0 the attribute produced a HAL link and an OpenAPI entry, but no route and no authorization rule: clients were told about an endpoint that answered 404. Reported at the operation attribute name.

Bad.

#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)]
#[operation(path = "publish", method = "POST")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
#[behavior(soft_delete)] // still mounts POST /films/{id}/restore
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub title: String,
}

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
use axum::{Json, Router, routing::post};
use ferra::{FerraError, FerraIdentity, Foundry, JwtConfig};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct MyClaims { sub: String }
impl FerraIdentity for MyClaims {
    fn id(&self) -> &str { &self.sub }
    fn has_role(&self, _role: &str) -> bool { false }
}
async fn publish_film() -> Result<Json<()>, FerraError> { Ok(Json(())) }
fn demo(conn: sea_orm::DatabaseConnection, jwt: JwtConfig) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
// The action route is yours, added to the router `Foundry::build()` returns:
let (builder, films) = Foundry::new(conn)
    .etag_key(std::env::var("ETAG_KEY")?)?
    .with_auth::<MyClaims>(jwt)
    .mount_and_handle::<Model>();
let app = builder.build().merge(
    Router::new()
        .route("/films/{id}/publish", post(publish_film))
        .with_state(films),
);
Ok(())
}
}

Fix. Remove the attribute. restore is the only named operation: it is mounted by #[behavior(soft_delete)] and governed by the restore key of #[authorize]. Write any other action route yourself and add it with .route(...) or .merge(...) on the value Foundry::build() returns (see custom-handlers.md). Ferra’s authorization does not cover a route you add: protect it yourself, as that page shows.

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_named_operation_refused.rs

FRG-340 — base_path has no leading slash

Trigger. FerraLayer::base_path("api"): the prefix does not start with /. Unlike the other codes of this page, this one is not raised by the derive but by an assert! in a const fn, and the message of the panic starts with the code: FRG-340: FerraLayer::base_path: the prefix must start with '/'. Called in a const (the usual place, const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = …), it is a compile error (“evaluation panicked”) at the literal; called in ordinary code, it panics when the line runs, which is at startup.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("api").build(); // no leading `/`
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("/api").build();
}

Fix. Start the prefix with /. See foundry.md § Sub-path mount.

Fixture. crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/fail_ferra_layer_base_path_no_leading_slash.rs

FRG-341 — base_path has a trailing slash

Trigger. FerraLayer::base_path("/api/"): the prefix ends with /. The links are built as <prefix>/<resource>/…, so a trailing slash would double it. Same mechanism and same two outcomes as FRG-340; the bare root "/" is this error too.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("/api/").build(); // trailing `/`
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("/api").build();
}

Fix. Drop the trailing /. For no prefix at all, do not call base_path.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]

use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().base_path("").build(); // empty
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]

use ferra::FerraLayer;
const APP_LAYER: FerraLayer = FerraLayer::new().build(); // no prefix
}

FRG-350 — #[field(filterable)] / #[field(sortable)] on a #[ferra(skip)] field

Trigger. A field declares #[field(filterable)] or #[field(sortable)] AND #[ferra(skip)] on the same declaration. The two markers contradict: #[ferra(skip)] removes the field from the API surface entirely (it does not appear in OpenAPI, requests, or responses), so a request cannot mention it as a filter or sort key — there is no surface to address. Per spec 011 FR-003, the framework refuses to compile a model that puts the field in both categories.

Why compile-time. The contradiction is decidable from the field’s declaration alone — no runtime input is needed. Constitution §III “Compile-Time over Runtime” forbids runtime checks for invariants the compiler can lift.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(skip)]
    #[field(filterable)] // contradicts skip: the field is not exposed
    pub internal_note: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix — expose the field.

Drop #[ferra(skip)] if the field should be exposed as a filterable column:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[field(filterable)]
    pub note: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix — keep the field internal.

Drop the filterable / sortable marker if the field should remain a server-internal column:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(skip)]
    pub internal_note: String,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

FRG-356 — a projection hides the cursor key or its tie-break key

Trigger. A model in cursor or both pagination mode has a projection whose read = [...] leaves out the #[field(cursor_key)] field, or the single primary key that breaks ties between equal cursor keys; or its cursor key is #[ferra(skip)] (and not the primary key), which the default read projection drops. The cursor token carries both values, so a projection that hides them would hand the client a field it cannot otherwise read. A write-only cursor key is FRG-354; this code is for a readable field that a projection omits. Reported at the cursor-key field, naming the projection and the field.

    pub id: i32,
    #[field(cursor_key, sortable)]
    pub rank: i64,
    pub title: String,

pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Reported at the identifier in read, naming the projection and the field. The deletion column of a soft-delete model is skip too, and is FRG-357; FRG-305 is the same rule for a write-only field.

FRG-359 — skip with write_only or computed, or on a primary key

Trigger. A field declares #[ferra(skip)] together with #[ferra(write_only)] or #[ferra(computed)], or declares skip or computed on a #[sea_orm(primary_key)] field. skip means the API neither reads nor writes the field; write_only and computed say the API writes it or fills it, and a key is the address of the row. Before 0.15.0 a skip + write_only field was left out of the description, the OpenAPI document and PATCH, yet a POST or a PUT on the bare path still wrote it: a declaration with no effect, and a field a client could set although the API said it did not exist. It is now refused. Reported at the skip (at the computed when there is no skip), naming the field.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "accounts")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(skip, write_only)] // hidden and writable at once
    pub secret: Option<String>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "accounts")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    #[ferra(write_only)] // written by clients, never returned
    pub secret: Option<String>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Fix. One code, and the help: line of the error names the fix for the trigger it found:

Triggerhelp:
skip with write_onlyremove skip to let clients write the field (write_only keeps it out of responses), or remove write_only to keep the field out of the API entirely
skip with computedremove skip to serve the computed value, or remove computed to keep the field out of the API entirely
skip on a primary keya primary key is the row’s identity and is in every link; remove skip
computed on a primary keya primary key is stored; remove computed

When several triggers hold on one field, the first row of the table is the one reported. See migrating-to-0.15.md if the model was relying on the old write.

Fixtures. frg_359_skip_write_only.rs, frg_359_skip_computed.rs, frg_359_skip_key.rs and frg_359_computed_key.rs, in crates/ferra-forge/tests/diagnostics/.

FRG-360 — a computed field without #[sea_orm(ignore)]

Trigger. A field declares #[ferra(computed)] and no #[sea_orm(ignore)]. A computed field has no column: Ferra fills it from FerraComputed and never reads or writes it in SQL. Sea-ORM only leaves a field out of its SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE when it is #[sea_orm(ignore)], so without the attribute the model still expects a column its table should not have. Reported at the computed, naming the field. A computed primary key is FRG-359, not this code.

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub subtotal: f64,
    #[ferra(computed)] // no `#[sea_orm(ignore)]`: the model expects a column
    pub total: Option<f64>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub subtotal: f64,
    #[sea_orm(ignore)] // no column
    #[ferra(computed)]
    pub total: Option<f64>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
impl ferra::compute::FerraComputed for Model {}
}

Fix. Add #[sea_orm(ignore)] above the field, and drop the column from your migration. The type must implement Default (Sea-ORM builds the ignored field with it). See migrating-to-0.15.md.

FRG-361 — filterable, sortable or cursor_key on a computed field

Trigger. A computed field also declares #[field(filterable)], #[field(sortable)] or #[field(cursor_key)]. These three put the field in a WHERE, an ORDER BY or a cursor, and a computed value is not in the database. One code for the three keys; the message names the key, and each key is reported at its own span. (skip and write_only fields have FRG-350 and FRG-354.)

Bad.

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub subtotal: f64,
    #[sea_orm(ignore)]
    #[ferra(computed)]
    #[field(sortable)] // the value is not in the database
    pub total: Option<f64>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]

    #[field(sortable)] // a stored column can be sorted

    #[sea_orm(ignore)]

Fix. Remove the named attribute from the computed field. To filter or sort on the value, store it in a column that a hook or a behavior keeps up to date, and put the attribute on that column.

FRG-362 — a computed field without impl FerraComputed

Trigger. A model has a #[ferra(computed)] field and no impl FerraComputed for Model. The derive writes that impl only for a model with no computed field, so that the application decides what each computed field is filled with; without one the model cannot be mounted. The derive asserts the bound on the first computed field, so the error is reported there, in Ferra’s words, and not only at Foundry::mount (where rustc adds its own Model: Mountable error after it).

error[E0277]: FRG-362: `Model` has a computed field but no `impl FerraComputed for Model`
  --> src/models/invoice.rs:21:9
   |
21 |     pub total: i64,
   |         ^^^^^ this model needs an `impl FerraComputed`, empty or not

Bad.

#![allow(unused)]

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub subtotal: f64,
    #[sea_orm(ignore)]
    #[ferra(computed)] // no `impl FerraComputed for Model` below

}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]

Good.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use ferra::FerraModel;
use ferra::compute::{FerraComputeError, FerraComputed};
use ferra::request_context::RequestContext;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[sea_orm(table_name = "invoices")]
#[ferra(auth = "none")]
pub struct Model {
    #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
    pub id: i32,
    pub subtotal: f64,
    #[sea_orm(ignore)]
    #[ferra(computed)]
    pub total: Option<f64>,
}
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
pub enum Relation {}
impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}

impl FerraComputed for Model {
    async fn compute_field(
        &mut self,
        field: ModelComputed,
        _ctx: &RequestContext,
    ) -> Result<(), FerraComputeError> {
        match field {
            ModelComputed::Total => self.total = Some(self.subtotal * 1.2),
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
}

Fix. Write impl ferra::compute::FerraComputed for Model, empty (impl FerraComputed for Model {}) when no field needs computing yet. Match on ModelComputed, the enum the derive writes next to the model with one variant per computed field. See Computed fields.

Fixtures. frg_362_computed_impl_missing.rs, in crates/ferra-forge/tests/diagnostics/, and fail_computed_without_impl.rs, which pins both errors in crates/ferra-http/tests/ui/.

FRG-363 — a HasMany or HasOne in a read list

Trigger. A projection’s read = [...] names a HasMany or a HasOne relation field of a model written with #[sea_orm::model]. The foreign key of such a relation is on the other side: it is served as the link to its sub-collection, never embedded, and a depth bound does not bound a fan-out (a HasOne has no bound either without a uniqueness the derive can see). A BelongsTo is the relation a read list embeds (Embedding); a name that is neither a field nor a relation is still FRG-301. Reported on the name inside read.

Bad.

use ferra::FerraModel;
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
mod film {
    use super::*;

    #[sea_orm::model]
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
    #[ferra(projection(name = "summary", read = [id, reviews]))] // `reviews` is a `HasMany`
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        #[sea_orm(has_many)]
        pub reviews: HasMany<super::review::Entity>,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

mod review {
    use super::*;

    #[sea_orm::model]
    #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "reviews")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        pub film_id: i32,
        #[sea_orm(belongs_to, from = "film_id", to = "id")]
        pub film: BelongsTo<super::film::Entity>,
    }

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}
fn main() {}

error: FRG-363: `reviews` is a relation whose foreign key is on the other side; it is served as the link `reviews` to its sub-collection, never embedded (a `HasOne` has no bound without a uniqueness the derive can see)

Fix. Remove the name from read. The relation is still in every response, as the link reviews to its sub-collection (Links and foreign keys). To show the rows of the other side inside this one, embed from that side: the BelongsTo of review to film is a name its read list may carry.

FRG-364 — an ignored field without computed

Trigger. A field declares #[sea_orm(ignore)] and no #[ferra(computed)]. A field with no column has no value to read from the table, and Sea-ORM builds it with Default. Ferra would serve that Default as if it were the row’s: a 0, an empty string, a null that lies. Since 0.16.0 the derive refuses the field instead of serving it (before 0.16.0 it compiled). Reported at the ignore, naming the field. #[ferra(computed)] on an ignored field is the supported form (FRG-360 is its converse).

Fix. Add #[ferra(computed)] and write the impl FerraComputed for Model that fills the field (empty when nothing computes it yet; see Computed fields), or move the field out of the model, into a type of your own or a Resource<M> route. See migrating-to-0.16.md.

FRG-365 — a composite foreign key

Trigger. A relation writes its from or its to as a list of columns, from = "(studio_id, studio_region)". Sea-ORM accepts the composite form; Ferra’s gate on a foreign key reads one column, so a model that compiled with a composite key had its key served to a caller who may not read the parent. Since 0.16.0 the derive refuses it instead (before 0.16.0 it compiled). Reported on the string, naming the key and the number of columns.

Ferra reads a from or a to as Sea-ORM does: "film_id", "Column::FilmId", "FilmId" and "filmId" all name the field film_id, and the gate follows each spelling. That holds for a from, matched against the fields of the model. A to names a field of the target, which the derive cannot see: it is read in snake_case ("FilmId" is film_id) and stays fail-closed. A to that then names no column of the target hides the key and refuses a write that names it; it never serves the key.

A to that names no field of the target is the same family. Ferra’s derive cannot see the target’s fields; it emits Column::<To> of the target on your string, so the check is rustc’s own: it reports it as E0599 on your string (and once more on #[sea_orm::model], Sea-ORM’s own), with no FRG-365 in its text. FRG-365 is the code to look up. A from that names no field of the model is Sea-ORM’s own refusal alone. Two fields with the same variant (line_2 and line2, both Line2) are refused by Sea-ORM itself (E0428).

Bad.

    #[ferra(auth = "bearer", client_pk)]

FRG-400 — two copies of Sea-ORM

Trigger. The application declares sea-orm in its own [dependencies], and cargo resolved that declaration and the one of ferra to different versions: the build holds two copies of the crate. Ferra’s routes read and write through ferra::sea_orm; every Sea-ORM type the application names is then a different type from the one Ferra expects. Without this code the compiler words it as “expected DatabaseConnection, found DatabaseConnection”, far from the cause. #[derive(FerraModel)] checks it, at the model, wherever the application’s sea-orm is there next to ferra, under the condition of the dependency itself:

  • sea-orm in [dependencies]: in every build;
  • sea-orm with optional = true: in the builds where one of the features that enable it is on (#[cfg(feature = "…")]: the implicit feature named like the dependency, or the features that write "dep:sea-orm" or "sea-orm/…");
  • sea-orm under [target.'cfg(…)'.dependencies]: where that cfg(…) holds;
  • sea-orm in [dev-dependencies]: under #[cfg(test)], which is the crate’s unit tests, integration tests (tests/) and benches. An example (examples/) has the dev-dependency too but nothing in the code tells it apart from the ordinary build, so there two copies show as the compiler’s own “expected DatabaseConnection, found DatabaseConnection”;
  • sea-orm under [target.<triple>.dependencies], named by a target triple and not by a cfg(…): no check, for the same reason.

Where the application’s copy is not there, the derive reaches Sea-ORM through ferra::sea_orm, and there is one copy to compare. A model with projections may add type errors of its own after FRG-400 under such a condition.

The rule: a Ferra project never holds two major versions of Sea-ORM, not even for its tests or an optional feature. The check is armed by the condition of the dependency, so a sea-orm = "1" that is only a dev-dependency, or only behind a feature (full = ["dep:sea-orm"]), is refused as soon as that condition holds (cargo test, --features full), next to a model written through the facade (use ferra::prelude::*;). Before 0.9.0 this compiled by accident; it is refused on purpose, because the model and Ferra’s routes would then speak of two different DatabaseConnections whenever the test or the feature is on. A declaration that is never active (a cfg(any()) table, an optional dependency no feature enables) is not a copy and is not refused. The remedy is the one below: give that sea-orm Ferra’s major, or remove it; cargo tree -d -i sea-orm (add --all-features for an optional one) lists the copies.

error[E0277]: FRG-400: the `sea-orm` your application declares is not the `sea-orm` Ferra was built with (`DatabaseConnection` is not `DatabaseConnection`)
   |         Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel, Serialize, Deserialize,
   |                                                         ^^^^^^^^^^ this model is written against another copy of `sea-orm` than the one Ferra's routes use

Bad.

[dependencies]
ferra   = { git = "https://github.com/ferra-rs/ferra", tag = "v0.17.0" } # built with sea-orm 2.x
sea-orm = "1"                                                           # another major

Good.

[dependencies]
ferra   = { git = "https://github.com/ferra-rs/ferra", tag = "v0.17.0" }
sea-orm = { version = "2.0", default-features = false, features = ["macros", "runtime-tokio-rustls", "sqlx-postgres"] }

Fix. Give sea-orm the same major version as Ferra, in [dependencies], [dev-dependencies] and under every feature (the CHANGELOG.md of each release says which), then check that one copy is left: cargo tree -d -i sea-orm prints nothing when it is. Or declare no sea-orm at all and write ferra::sea_orm::… (put use ferra::prelude::*; or use ferra::sea_orm; at the top of each file that uses a Sea-ORM derive). sea-orm-migration, if the project has migrations, follows the same major.

Fixture. crates/ferra-forge/tests/ui/fail_two_sea_orm_copies.rs pins the message. A second copy of a crate cannot be built inside a fixture, so it uses two stand-in types; that the derive emits the bound, and that it holds when there is one copy, is shown by crates/ferra/tests/sea_orm_direct_style.rs.

Custom handlers

Most Ferra apps need at least one route that is not pure CRUD — a publish verb, a derived collection, an aggregation, a webhook receiver. This page is the authoritative guide to writing those handlers on top of a Ferra-served API. A reader with this page plus standard Rust knowledge produces a compiling custom handler on the first attempt — no framework source, no ADR, no constitution required.

The companion CRUD / envelope / Tower-stack / typed-extraction reference is ferra-http.md. The router-assembly facade is foundry.md.

Dependencies. The examples on this page assume the dependencies of Getting started:

[dependencies]
ferra   = { git = "https://github.com/ferra-rs/ferra", tag = "v0.17.0" }
sea-orm = { version = "2.0", default-features = false, features = ["macros", "runtime-tokio-rustls", "sqlx-postgres"] }
tokio   = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
axum    = "0.8"
serde   = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }

When the generated routes are not enough

The five built-in handlers cover the resource-shaped endpoints — list, read, create, update, delete. They are all you need for ~80 % of the surface a typical app exposes.

You write a custom handler when the route is not one of those five operations. Common reasons:

  • Verbs on a resource. POST /films/{id}/publish, POST /invoices/{id}/cancel, POST /accounts/{id}/transfer — verbs on a resource that aren’t expressible as PUT. A verb on one row of one model is a declared action first: Ferra serves it with its own rule, the row lock, the preconditions and the write of a PUT. Write a handler of your own when the route is not a verb on one row: a collection, a webhook, an aggregate.
  • Derived collections. GET /films/popular, GET /actors/{id}/films — collections whose membership is computed, not just SELECT * WHERE ....
  • Multi-resource projections. GET /dashboard returning a join of three resources at once.
  • Webhook receivers. POST /webhooks/stripe reading a non-Ferra payload shape.
  • Cross-cutting endpoints. GET /healthz, GET /metrics.

Custom handlers are plain Axum handlers. They accept Axum extractors, return Result<_, FerraError> for RFC 7807 error continuity, and compose with the framework router by appending .route(...) or .merge(...) on the value Foundry::build() returns.

The worked example: POST /films/{id}/publish

The complete shape of a custom handler for a verb on one row — model declaration, handler signature, composition with Foundry — in one file. The route reaches the films table through Resource<Film>: it is judged by the rules of PUT /films/{id}, not by whatever the handler remembers to check. Drop this into a fresh src/main.rs whose Cargo.toml declares the canonical dependency set (ferra, tokio, serde, sea-orm as in Getting Started, and axum with its macros feature, which #[axum::debug_handler] needs) and it compiles. The route is a custom handler, not a declared action: for a verb that Ferra serves itself, with its own rule, the row lock and the preconditions, see Declared actions.

use axum::{
    Json, Router,
    http::{StatusCode, header},
    response::{IntoResponse, Response},
    routing::post,
};
use ferra::{
    ClaimCheck, Date, FerraError, FerraIdentity, FerraJson, FerraModel, FerraPath, Foundry,
    HmacAlgorithm, JwtConfig, Resource, ResourceHandle,
};
use sea_orm::entity::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

// --- The model -----------------------------------------------------

mod film {
    use super::*;

    #[derive(
        Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq,
        DeriveEntityModel, FerraModel,
        Serialize, Deserialize,
    )]
    #[sea_orm(table_name = "films")]
    #[ferra(auth = "bearer")] // the posture every model declares; see ferra-auth.md
    #[authorize(              // a film belongs to the caller who created it
        list = IsOwner,
        get = IsOwner,
        create = Authenticated,
        update = IsOwner,
        delete = IsOwner
    )]
    pub struct Model {
        #[sea_orm(primary_key)]
        pub id: i32,
        #[sea_orm(unique)]
        pub title: String,
        pub director: String,
        pub year: Option<i32>,
        pub release_date: Option<Date>,
        pub published: bool,
        #[field(owner)]
        pub owner_id: Uuid,
    }

    #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, EnumIter, DeriveRelation)]
    pub enum Relation {}

    impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}
}

pub use film::Model as Film;

// --- Who the caller is ---------------------------------------------

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Deserialize)]
struct Claims {
    sub: String,
}

impl FerraIdentity for Claims {
    fn id(&self) -> &str {
        &self.sub
    }
    fn has_role(&self, _role: &str) -> bool {
        false
    }
}

// --- The handler's request body -------------------------------------

// Plain serde struct — nothing Ferra-specific. The `FerraJson<T>`
// extractor on the handler signature accepts any `T: DeserializeOwned`.
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct PublishRequest {
    release_date: Option<Date>,
}

// --- The handler's response body ------------------------------------

// A route of your own answers with a body of its own: the fields you
// choose, under the names you choose.
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct PublishedFilm {
    id: i32,
    title: String,
    published: bool,
    release_date: Option<Date>,
}

// --- The handler ---------------------------------------------------

// `#[axum::debug_handler]` is optional but turns the dense
// `Handler` trait-bound error into a single, targeted message
// when one of the rules below is violated. Keep it on while
// iterating; it is a no-op at runtime.
#[axum::debug_handler(state = ResourceHandle<Film>)]
async fn publish_film(
    // FromRequestParts — binds the caller (the bearer token) and gives
    //                   access to the films, under the films' rules.
    films: Resource<Film>,
    // FromRequestParts — `FerraPath` is the typed-extraction
    //                   wrapper around `axum::extract::Path<T>`.
    FerraPath(id): FerraPath<i32>,
    // FromRequest — `FerraJson` consumes the request body. Body-
    //              consuming extractors MUST be the LAST argument.
    FerraJson(body): FerraJson<PublishRequest>,
) -> Result<Response, FerraError> {
    // Same rules as `PUT /films/{id}`: another caller's film is a 404 and
    // the row is unchanged. Only `published` and `release_date` are written.
    let patch = film::ModelPatch {
        published: Some(true),
        release_date: body.release_date.map(Some),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    let Some(film) = films.update(id, patch).await? else {
        // Written, but this caller may not read the row: the route sends no body.
        return Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT.into_response());
    };

    // Answer with the fields this handler exposes.
    Ok(Json(PublishedFilm {
        id: film.id,
        title: film.title,
        published: film.published,
        release_date: film.release_date,
    })
    .into_response())
}

// A create is the same shape: `201` and a `Location` for a caller who may read the
// row, `201` with no body and no `Location` for one who may not.
async fn create_film(
    films: Resource<Film>,
    FerraJson(new): FerraJson<film::ModelWriteProjection>,
) -> Result<Response, FerraError> {
    let Some(created) = films.create(new).await? else {
        // Written, but this caller may not read the row: 201, no body, no `Location`.
        return Ok(StatusCode::CREATED.into_response());
    };
    let location = format!("/films/{}", created.id);
    Ok((
        StatusCode::CREATED,
        [(header::LOCATION, location)],
        Json(created),
    )
        .into_response())
}

// --- Composition with Foundry --------------------------------------

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let database_url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL")?;
    let conn = sea_orm::Database::connect(&database_url).await?;

    let jwt = JwtConfig::single_secret(
        "key-1",
        std::env::var("JWT_SECRET")?,
        HmacAlgorithm::Hs256,
        ClaimCheck::expect("https://auth.example.com/"),
        ClaimCheck::expect("films-api"),
    )?;

    // `mount_and_handle` mounts `Film` as `.mount::<Film>()` does — the CRUD
    // routes, the JWT layer — and returns the handle that routes of your own
    // use to reach the films.
    let (foundry, films) = Foundry::new(conn)
        .etag_key(std::env::var("ETAG_KEY")?)?
        .with_auth::<Claims>(jwt)
        .mount_and_handle::<Film>();
    let api = foundry.with_docs().build();

    // The custom handler lives on a sibling sub-router whose state is the
    // handle. `ResourceHandle<M>: Clone` (reference counts only).
    let custom = Router::new()
        .route("/films/{id}/publish", post(publish_film))
        .route("/films/add", post(create_film))
        .with_state(films);

    let app = api.merge(custom);

    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("0.0.0.0:3000").await?;
    // The rate limiter keys on the peer address: serve with connect info.
    axum::serve(listener, app.into_make_service_with_connect_info::<std::net::SocketAddr>()).await?;
    Ok(())
}

film::ModelPatch is the struct #[derive(FerraModel)] generates next to Model ({Model}Patch, one Option<T> per writable field, None leaving the column; also <Film as FerraViews>::Patch); the struct is unchanged by the PATCH route of 0.14.0, which reads the same Value it serializes to. The owner column is compared with the token’s sub rendered as a string, so a Uuid owner_id matches a sub holding that UUID (ferra-auth.md).

create and update return an Option of the read view. Some is the row, written and readable by this caller: publish_film answers 200 with it, create_film answers 201 with a Location and the row. None is a row written that this caller may not read, under the rule of the generated route (the get rule, then the authority’s can(Get)): publish_film answers 204 with no body, and create_film answers 201 with no body, no Location and no id in any header, as the generated routes do for that caller. The Location is built in the Some arm only, so a caller who may not read the row learns nothing of its key. None is never an error: a refused or invalid write stays an Err, and the absent row’s 404 with it (ferra-http.md).

update does what PATCH /films/{id} does (RFC 7396): None leaves the column, and a JSON object set on a stored JSON object is merged into it instead of replacing it (a null member removes its key). A null set on a field that cannot be null (Some(serde_json::Value::Null) on a required JSON field) is the 422 required.

Resource<Film> has six methods — get, list, list_cursor, create, update, delete — each of which does what the generated route of the same name does: it runs the authorization checkpoint of the operation, scopes a list to the caller’s rows under IsOwner, stamps the owner on create, validates with the model’s #[field(...)] rules, and writes under the owner’s guard. What it hands back is the model’s read view, <Film as FerraViews>::Read: a #[ferra(write_only)] column is not a member of that type, so a route cannot send it by mistake. create and update hand back an Option of it: None where the generated route sends no body, because the row is written and the caller may not read it (a create then answers 201 with no body, no Location and no id in any header). ferra-http.md is the reference.

Field rules reach a route of your own (0.13.0). A field with a #[field(read = …, write = …)] rule is judged for the bound caller by Resource<M> as it is by the generated routes. What get, list and list_cursor return has each field the caller may not read set to None, so a route that serializes it sends no such key (never null); an IsOwner read rule is judged row by row. A gated field of the write view, and of a patch, is an Option (Option<Option<T>> when the column is nullable): None is left alone, Some(None) is null, and a field the caller may not read or write that you set is refused like the generated route refuses it (422, then 403), the row unchanged. A filter on a field the caller may not read is refused as on the route, and a sort on it keeps the default order.

Hooks (0.13.0). Resource<M>::create and Resource<M>::update run the model’s before_save and after_save hooks, and Resource<M>::delete its before_delete and after_delete, in the write’s transaction, as the generated routes do (Hooks).

A write the database keeps aborting (0.16.0). A Resource<M> write that the database aborted on each of its three attempts returns Err(FerraError::RetryExhausted): return it from your route and the client gets the 503 retry_exhausted with Retry-After: 1. Never replay the write in a loop of your own; the retries already ran (Transient conflicts are retried).

A route of your own that writes twice (0.17.0). The request budget is one per request, not one per write. After the first write has committed, the rest of the request is no longer cut: a second write has no deadline before its COMMIT, and its retry is bounded by the three attempts only. The after_commit of every write of the request shares one post-commit deadline, max(deadline, first post-commit work + 1 s) (After commit). So the after_commit of a later write can be cut at once, and its Resource<M> call then returns Err while that write is committed. A 503 service_unavailable (no connection in time) or retry_exhausted met by a later write speaks for the operation given up, not for the request: the earlier write stands, and a client must not retry a non-idempotent request blindly (RFC 9110 § 9.2.2). Keep one write per route of your own. If a route must write twice, make a replay safe with the idempotent create recipe, and never send the client an error that tells it nothing was written.

No response envelope in 0.9.0. The routes Foundry generates answer with the row filtered through its read projection, under its wire names, flat or with HAL _links as the client’s Accept chooses. That envelope is not public: a route of your own would build links that know neither the base path, nor the version prefix, nor the configured origin. Answer with a struct of your own, as above. The same goes for #[ferra(rename_all = "camelCase")]: the read view carries the model’s Rust field names, so a route that serializes it sends those, not the wire names of the generated routes.

A successful POST /films/42/publish with body {"release_date": "2026-05-10"} returns 200 OK:

{
  "id": 42,
  "title": "Rust en pratique",
  "published": true,
  "release_date": "2026-05-10"
}

Errors flow through the same FerraError taxonomy the built-in handlers use — a malformed JSON body returns 400 with type: "https://ferra.rs/errors/validation"; a film that is not yours returns 404 with type: "https://ferra.rs/errors/not_found", the same answer as a film that does not exist; no token is a 401. Clients that handle one Ferra error already handle this one.

Extractor ordering: FromRequest vs FromRequestParts

Axum has two extractor traits. The distinction looks academic until you write your first multi-extractor handler — then it becomes the load-bearing rule.

TraitReads fromExamplesPosition
FromRequestPartsrequest parts only (method, URI, headers, state)State<T>, Path<T>, Query<T>, Parts, HeaderMap, FerraPath<T>any position
FromRequestthe whole request, including the body (consumed)Json<T>, Bytes, String, Form<T>, FerraJson<T>last argument only

The rule: at most one body-consuming extractor (FromRequest) per handler, and it MUST be the last argument. Every other extractor is body-agnostic (FromRequestParts) and goes earlier.

This is a fundamental property of HTTP, not an Axum design quirk: a request body is a one-shot stream. Once you have read it, the bytes are gone.

The handler in the worked example follows the rule:

async fn publish_film(
    films: Resource<Film>,                    // FromRequestParts
    FerraPath(id): FerraPath<i32>,            // FromRequestParts
    FerraJson(body): FerraJson<PublishRequest>, // FromRequest — LAST
) -> Result<...> { ... }

(An excerpt of the handler above, which is the compiled version.)

Reorder FerraJson ahead of FerraPath and the build fails. Without #[axum::debug_handler] the compiler reports the violation through a deep trait-bound chain on Handler. With #[axum::debug_handler] the diagnostic points directly at the offending argument.

Multiple body extractors. Axum allows exactly one body-consuming extractor per handler. If you legitimately need to look at the raw bytes and a typed JSON deserialization, do both inside a single FromRequest-implementing wrapper, or read Bytes and parse it explicitly with serde_json::from_slice. There is no Json<A> + Json<B> shape.

Send + Sync + 'static: the bound-set cheat-sheet

Tokio runs handlers on a multi-threaded executor by default. Every value Axum carries through the handler must be sendable across threads and outlive the request. The compiler enforces this through Send + Sync + 'static-shaped bounds on the Handler trait — failures here look daunting at first read.

The cheat-sheet:

SymptomLikely causeFix
the trait Send is not implemented for ... inside an async fna !Send value is held across an .await (Rc<_>, RefCell<_>, MutexGuard from std::sync::Mutex)use Arc<_>, tokio::sync::Mutex, or restructure so the offending value is dropped before the .await
the trait Sync is not implemented for ... on State<T>the state type is not Sync (e.g., it owns a non-Sync cache)wrap the inner shared state in Arc<RwLock<...>> or restructure to a channel
argument requires that ... must outlive 'staticthe handler captures a non-'static reference (&str from outside the closure, a borrow from the request)own the data (String, Bytes), or extract it via an extractor
Handler<_, _> not satisfied with a long, hard-to-read chainusually one of the three above, hidden behind Handler’s blanket impladd #[axum::debug_handler] and read the first targeted error it produces

Notes on the framework’s own types:

  • ResourceHandle<M> is Clone + Send + Sync + 'static — it wraps a shared connection. Keep it in the router state and pass it through any number of handlers freely.
  • FerraJson<T> / FerraPath<T> add no bounds beyond the inner T: DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static that Axum already requires.
  • FerraError is Send + Sync + 'static and implements axum::response::IntoResponse — return Result<_, FerraError> from any handler signature.

If your handler async fn body holds a !Send value across an .await, the bound failure surfaces in the Handler impl, not in the body. Move the value into a synchronous block or drop it before the await.

Friendlier diagnostics with #[axum::debug_handler]

Axum’s Handler trait has a blanket impl that erases per-argument type information by the time the bound failure is reported. Without help, a single wrong extractor produces a multi-screen not satisfied chain.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use axum::Json;
use ferra::{FerraError, FerraPath};

#[axum::debug_handler]
async fn my_handler(FerraPath(id): FerraPath<i32>) -> Result<Json<i32>, FerraError> {
    Ok(Json(id))
}
}

The proc-macro re-checks the arguments one by one and emits a single targeted error per offending argument:

  • Json must be the last extractor
  • the trait FromRequestParts is not implemented for …
